ideas.trigger: sme: deep-dive on request — largest BSE SME IPO index member (weight 6.79%), FY26 revenue +76% / PAT +75%, stock +677% over the ₹136 issue price, ₹168 cr preferential issue at ₹853 announced 23/26-Sep-2026
ideas.thesis:
**In plain words.**
- **Growing fast:** sales have grown about 80% a year for three years (₹303 cr in FY26) and profit is growing just as fast.
- **But growth is eating cash:** after two years of growth the business still takes in less cash than it spends, mostly because unsold stock keeps piling up.
- **The price already assumes a lot:** at about 79x last year's profit, the company must hit its targets for roughly 2–3 more years just to justify today's price.
- **One big risk:** almost all its scooters are the slow, no-licence kind. If the government tightens those rules, the core business is hit.
- **Things to watch:** heavy use of imported parts, a pending customs demand, sharp pay rises for the owning family, and a stock that is hard to sell quickly.
- The next real test is the half-year results due by mid-November 2026.

### 1. What the company is
- A family-run electric-scooter maker in Hisar, Haryana, incorporated 15-Jul-2021. The Arya family (Niraj — chairman; Deepak — whole-time director; Kunal — MD) owns 72.77%.
- **Core product:** low-speed scooters (under 25 km/h) that need no registration and no licence, sold at about ₹50–75k. Brands: Zelio (Eeva, Gracy, Mystery, X-Men, Little Gracy) and Tanga (electric three-wheelers: Butterfly, SS, e-Loader; about 800 units in FY26). Two faster models are promised for FY27.
- **How it makes them:** it assembles imported kits. FY26 imports were ₹199 cr against ₹233 cr of materials used, so roughly 85% of content is imported (our calculation). R&D spending is nil per the annual report. About 30% localised, target 80%.
- **Sales network:** 400+ dealers in 25+ states, about 70% exclusive; target 550+ in FY27.
- Subsidiary Zelio Auto Components Ltd (incorporated May 2025, component trading). CEO Divyanshu Agarwal (ex-Navi) from 15-Apr-2026; CFO Shubham Garg.

### 2. Growth
Standalone, audited; units are the MD's statements, not audited.

| | FY22 | FY23 | FY24 | FY25 | FY26 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Revenue (₹ cr) | 12.9 | 51.3 | 94.4 | 172.2 | **303.5** |
| Units sold | 3k+ | 10k+ | 21k+ | 38k+ | **70k+** |
| Profit after tax (₹ cr) | — | 3.1 | 6.3 | 16.0 | **28.0** |

- About 81% a year revenue growth FY23→FY26. FY26: revenue +76%, profit +75%. The "82% growth" headline mixes consolidated and standalone figures; like for like it is 76%.
- Consolidated FY26: revenue ₹310.71 cr, PAT ₹28.39 cr, EPS ₹15.14.

| Margin | FY25 | FY26 |
|---|---:|---:|
| Gross margin | 23.1% | 23.5% |
| Operating margin (EBITDA ex other income, our calculation) | 12.2% | 11.3% |

- Margins are steady, not expanding. The company's quoted 12.2% for FY26 includes other income.
- Price per vehicle about ₹43k (₹303.5 cr ÷ 70k units), consistent with the ₹44k an analyst quoted on the call.
- One wobble: Q4 FY26 revenue works out to about ₹78.6 cr, below Q3's ₹91.6 cr (derived as H2 minus the company's Q3 update, so the two may not be on exactly the same basis).

### 3. Quality of that growth — the weak spot
| | FY25 | FY26 |
|---|---:|---:|
| Cash from operations, standalone (₹ cr) | −6.9 (restated) | −7.4 |
| Cash from operations, consolidated (₹ cr) | — | −11.2 |
| Inventory (₹ cr) | 31.6 | 55.3 |
| Short-term loans and advances (₹ cr) | 13.9 | 42.6 |

- Growth is eating cash. Inventory is up 75% (about 87 days of sales). Of the ₹42.6 cr of advances, about ₹22.5 cr was paid to suppliers in advance and about ₹19 cr is GST/customs refunds due.
- Balance sheet strong since the IPO: debt ₹18.6 cr against ₹26 cr cash and ₹111 cr equity. ₹25 cr of IPO money was still unspent in fixed deposits at March 2026.
- New plants cost almost nothing (Cuttack under ₹3 cr, Coimbatore up to ₹1 cr): low spending, but also a model rivals can copy easily.

### 4. Future scope
- **Company guidance** (not independently checked): FY27 revenue growth of 75–80% (≈ ₹530–560 cr), 125,000+ scooters and 2,000+ three-wheelers. In Nov-2025 it was guiding only ₹350–400 cr, so the target has been raised sharply.
- **Capacity:** about 240,000 units a year after Coimbatore; utilisation about 40% at March 2026. Factory space is not the limit — demand and dealers are.
- **The market:** the company puts the low-speed segment at 8–10 lakh units a year and claims 4–5% share in H1 FY26, targeting more than 10% in FY27. Nobody independently tracks this market; low-speed scooters never appear in VAHAN, so the claimed share cannot be verified.
- For context, registered electric two-wheelers were 14.0 lakh in FY26 (+22%); TVS, Bajaj, Ather and Vida hold about 76% — a different segment from Zelio's.

**New money: ₹168 cr at ₹853 a share** (shareholder vote 20-Oct-2026)

| Allottee | Instrument | Amount |
|---|---|---:|
| Motilal Oswal Financial Services | shares | ~₹40 cr |
| Calliope Capital (Navin Agarwal) | shares | ~₹31 cr |
| Param Value Investments (Mukul Agrawal) | shares | ~₹8.5 cr |
| Hem Growth Opportunities Fund | shares | ~₹3 cr |
| Niraj, Deepak and Kunal Arya (promoters) | warrants | ₹85 cr |

- For expansion including the Patan three-wheeler plant (no commissioning filing found for Patan).

### Bull case vs bear case
| Bull | Bear |
|---|---|
| A first mover in a fast-growing but ignored low-speed segment | An assembler of imported kits with no R&D |
| Growing about 80% a year with a clean balance sheet | Growth consumes cash; operating cash flow negative two years running |
| Cheap capacity to add; plants cost ₹1–3 cr | Depends on a regulatory exemption for low-speed scooters |
| Credible investors buying in at ₹853 | Poor governance signals; 79x earnings in an illiquid, surveillance-flagged stock |

| # | Risk | Detail |
|---:|---|---|
| 1 | Rules | The business relies on the low-speed exemption from registration. A tightening, or a crackdown on scooters modified to go faster, hits the core product. No government subsidy (MD). |
| 2 | Imports and customs | About 85% imported content, largely China. Customs show-cause notice (29-Jul-2026) proposes ₹6.72 cr of extra duty plus interest and a penalty on FY23–24 kit imports; disclosed late (the company said the email went to spam). |

ideas.name: Umiya Mobile Ltd
ideas.trigger: sme: deep-dive on request — BSE SME multi-brand smartphone retailer (401 stores claimed), FY26 revenue +49% / PAT +67%, stock +74.7% in 3 months and +48% in a month after the Jul-2026 lock-in release
ideas.thesis:
**In plain words.**
- **What it is:** a Rajkot-based chain that sells smartphones (97% of sales) through its own stores and a much larger network of partner-run "retail outlets" in Gujarat, Maharashtra and Madhya Pradesh.
- **Growth looks strong:** FY26 sales ₹836 cr (+49%), profit ₹9.2 cr (+67%), and the store count went from 219 to about 400 in a year.
- **But the profit is not from selling phones.** The company booked ₹48.2 cr of brand rebates ("discount income") as other income, against a profit before tax of only ₹12.3 cr. Before those rebates, operating EBITDA was **−₹33.2 cr** — the company's own June-2026 presentation says so.
- **Cash flow is flattered:** the reported +₹3.0 cr operating cash flow includes the ₹21.1 cr IPO share premium added back as an "operating" inflow. Without it, operating cash flow was about −₹18.1 cr (our calculation). FY25 was −₹15.2 cr.
- **A large, unexplained deposit:** ₹51.7 cr of interest-free "deposit for branch management" sits on the balance sheet — more than the company's entire net worth of ₹48.4 cr. How it works is not described anywhere we read.
- **Cheap on the headline P/E (13.5x), but the quality flags are many:** bank statements that did not match the books, a very cheap auditor replaced after the listing year, two BSE price-movement queries, ESM surveillance, and 37 lakh promoter shares freed from lock-in in July 2026.

### 1. What the company is
- BSE SME only: scrip 544464, symbol UML, ISIN INE1P1A01018, listed 4-Aug-2025. Registered office Gondal Road, Rajkot. No subsidiaries.
- Store brands: Umiya Mobile, MyPhone, Phone Plus, Phone & Phone, and Leela Mobile (new, 21-May-2026). A Vivo exclusive store opened Sep-2025. No e-commerce disclosed.
- About 70% of sales are on EMI/financing (MD on the call). B2B was 26.8% of FY26 revenue per the presentation — the CFO said "more than 73%" on the call, which contradicts it.
- Promoters are three brothers: Kishorbhai P. Jadwani (Chairman & MD), Girishkumar P. Jadvani and Vijesh P. Patel (whole-time directors). CFO Piyush J. Dedakiya.

**FY26 revenue mix (₹ cr)**

| Category | FY26 | Share |
|---|---:|---:|
| Mobiles | 807.61 | 96.6% |
| Accessories | 10.66 | 1.3% |
| Home appliances | 9.13 | 1.1% |
| Laptops / tablets | 8.70 | 1.0% |

**Store count**

| Date | Stores | Detail |
|---|---:|---|
| Jul-2025 (prospectus) | 219 | 20 owned + 199 retail outlets; 44 cities |
| 26-Sep-2025 | 255 | announcement |
| Nov-2025 | 268 | investor presentation |
| Jun-2026 | 401 | 30 owned + 371 retail outlets, 12 warehouses |
| Jul-2026 | 390 | annual report (Gujarat 197, Maharashtra 127, MP 65, UT 1) — conflicts with June's 401 |

- FY26 revenue by channel: owned stores ₹438.4 cr, retail outlets ₹397.7 cr.
- Company-claimed store economics: capex ₹35–40 lakh and working capital ₹60–70 lakh per store, payback 6–12 months, ₹25–30 lakh sales a month per store. Unverified — that run-rate implies ₹1,200 cr+ a year, not the ₹836 cr reported.

### 2. Growth — and where the profit comes from
| ₹ cr | FY23 | FY24 | FY25 | FY26 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Sales (ex purchase allowance) | 311.90 | 424.08 | 560.08 | **836.10** |
| Brand rebates ("purchase allowance" / "discount income") | 21.41 | 27.40 | 41.09 | **48.20** |
| EBITDA incl. rebates (company) | 1.84 | 5.76 | 10.94 | 15.14 |
| Profit before tax | 0.26 | 3.15 | 7.42 | 12.29 |
| Profit after tax | 0.18 | 2.35 | 5.51 | **9.19** |

- FY26 sales +49.3%; FY23→FY26 sales grew about 39% a year; PAT +67%.
- In the prospectus the rebate sat inside revenue from operations; in the FY26 accounts it moved to other income. Either way, it is larger than the entire profit.
- FY25 PAT conflicts between sources: ₹5.51 cr audited vs ₹5.66 cr restated.

| Margin | FY25 | FY26 |
|---|---:|---:|
| Trading gross margin incl. rebates (our calc) | 6.6% | 7.1% |
| Trading gross margin ex rebates (our calc) | −0.7% | 1.4% |
| EBITDA margin incl. rebates | 2.0% | 1.8% |
| Operating EBITDA ex rebates (company, Jun-2026) | — | −₹33.18 cr |

**Half-years (₹ cr)**

| | H2 FY25 | H1 FY26 | H2 FY26 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Revenue | 308.68 | 365.19 | 470.91 |
| Profit after tax | 2.02 | 3.78 | 5.41 |

### 3. Balance sheet and cash — the weak spot
| ₹ cr, 31-Mar | FY25 | FY26 |
|---|---:|---:|
| Net worth | 14.32 | 48.39 |
| Inventory | 67.27 | 106.85 |
| Trade payables | 26.79 | 49.15 |
| Short-term debt (bank + director) | 23.36 | 6.33 |
| Deposit for branch management (interest-free) | 30.66 | **51.74** |
| Cash (of which cash in hand) | — | 3.54 (3.41) |
| Operating cash flow, reported | −15.16 | +2.98 |
| Operating cash flow ex IPO premium add-back (our calc) | −15.16 | ≈ −18.1 |

- Branch-management deposit history: ₹9.63 cr (FY23) → ₹16.04 cr (FY24) → ₹30.66 cr (FY25) → ₹51.74 cr (FY26).
- Inventory is about 47 days of cost of goods (our calc) against the company's claim of 15–30 days.
- Also on the FY26 balance sheet: GST receivable ₹26.33 cr, rebate receivable ₹7.46 cr, a Bajaj deposit ₹3.56 cr; receivables ₹6.55 cr, of which ₹1.23 cr is over a year old.
- FY26 capex ₹2.62 cr (including a "Baroda" trademark at ₹25 lakh); an "other inflow" of ₹18.14 cr in investing is unexplained.

### 4. Future scope
- Store roll-out is the growth engine: Madhya Pradesh entry in Jan-2026 (10 stores in two days), a new Leela Mobile brand, and the Vivo exclusive format.
- Industry backdrop: India shipped 152 million smartphones in 2025 (+0.5%), with offline at 57% and rising (IDC). Q2 2026 shipments fell 11.1% on a memory-chip shortage while average prices rose 14.4% and offline share reached 58.1%.
- Offline's rising share helps a store chain; flat-to-falling unit volumes and dependence on brand rebates hurt it.

### Bull case vs bear case
| Bull | Bear |
|---|---|
| Fast store roll-out: 219 → ~400 in a year across three states | Profit is smaller than the brand rebates; operating EBITDA is negative without them |
| Offline retail is gaining share of Indian smartphone sales | Operating cash flow is negative once the IPO premium add-back is removed |
| 13.5x headline P/E and 0.15x sales, well below listed peers | ₹51.7 cr branch deposit of unknown terms is bigger than net worth |
| IPO money cut bank debt from ₹23.4 cr to ₹6.3 cr | Bank-statement mismatches, a ₹1.5 lakh auditor replaced, ESM surveillance, lock-in overhang |

ideas.name: Presstonic Engineering Ltd
ideas.trigger: sme: deep-dive on request — NSE Emerge metro-interiors supplier; ₹115.09 cr Titagarh order (≈2.8x FY26 revenue) won Feb-2026; stock +75% in five sessions (₹29.95 → ₹52.50, 18–25 Sep-2026) around a new Titagarh Surat Metro order
ideas.thesis:
**In plain words.**
- **What it is:** a Bengaluru sheet-metal and aluminium job-shop that makes seats, grab poles, handrails and cable ducts for metro and railway coach builders (BEML, Titagarh, CRRC, CAF, ICF). Not an auto stamping business.
- **The big positive:** in Feb-2026 Titagarh awarded it a **₹115.09 cr** contract for Mumbai Metro Lines 5 and 6 (saloon interiors for 240 cars, delivered May-2026 to Nov-2028) — about 2.8 times the company's entire FY26 revenue of ₹40.5 cr.
- **The big problem: FY26 profit depends on an accounting choice.** It capitalised ₹5.73 cr of "Branding" as an intangible asset. FY26 profit before tax was only ₹3.17 cr — had the branding been expensed, FY26 would have been a pre-tax loss of about ₹2.5 cr (our arithmetic). Indian GAAP generally does not allow a company to capitalise its own brand; whether it was bought or built is not stated.
- **Cash keeps going out:** operating cash flow was negative three years running (−₹1.4 cr, −₹3.2 cr, −₹6.5 cr), and most of the ₹26.4 cr rights-issue money went into ₹17.4 cr of advances to unnamed suppliers.
- **Ownership changed hands:** promoters took up only half their rights, falling from 58% to 44%; a single non-promoter investor, Pushpa Bhaju, now holds about 13%.
- **History of disclosure problems:** SEBI found the IPO prospectus hid a director's cheque-bounce conviction and fined the lead manager; NSE cautioned the company for late disclosure.
- **Cheap on sales (2x) but expensive on clean earnings.** The stock is −14% since its 2023 IPO after adjusting for the rights issue, and has more than doubled from its July-2026 low.

### 1. What the company is
- Listed on NSE Emerge (SME) on 18-Dec-2023; symbol PRESSTONIC, ISIN INE0R1601012. Two leased plants in Bengaluru: Sunkadakatte (~28,300 sq ft) and Peenya (~33,200 sq ft, production from 8-Nov-2024). Owns no property. 44 employees on the rolls, 194 people in total.
- Promoters: MD Herga Poornachandra Kedilaya and JMD & CFO Yermal Giridhar Rao (each 21.99%). No subsidiaries.
- Products: metro/rail saloon seats, grab poles, handrails, emergency ramps, luggage racks, aluminium cable ducts, under-frame modules, battery boxes, driver cabins, signalling enclosures; plus infrastructure fabrication (incl. solar structures), stainless general fabrication, US commercial-kitchen oven parts (Alto-Shaam), and a first defence-type job (L&T hydraulic tanks).
- Certifications: EN 15085-2 welding upgraded to CL1 (Sep-2026); EN 17460 adhesive bonding (Oct-2024).

**FY26 segments (first time reported)**

| Segment | Revenue (₹ cr) | Share |
|---|---:|---:|
| Metro rail components | 19.37 | 47.8% |
| General stainless fabrication | 8.60 | 21.2% |
| Infrastructure engineering | 8.55 | 21.1% |
| Others | 3.99 | 9.8% |

- Exports ₹4.42 cr in FY26 (10.9% of revenue), up from ₹1.22 cr (5.8%).
- Customer concentration at IPO: top-5 customers were 99.8% of FY23 revenue and 99.2% of H1 FY24; not disclosed since.

### 2. Growth
| ₹ cr | FY21 | FY22 | FY23 | FY24 | FY25 | FY26 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Revenue | 7.61 | 12.63 | 21.03 | 26.19 | 21.04 | **40.50** |
| EBITDA ex other income (our calc) | 2.93 | 3.01 | 6.96 | — | 4.63 | 7.15 |
| EBITDA margin | 38% | 24% | 33% | — | 22.0% | 17.7% |
| Profit before tax | −0.22 | 0.21 | 3.56 | 2.67 | 0.89 | 3.17 |
| Profit after tax | −0.17 | 0.14 | 2.56 | 2.53 | 0.86 | **2.60** |

- FY21–FY23 are restated prospectus figures; FY24–FY26 audited. FY26 revenue +92.5% on FY25, but FY25 was itself down 20% after a collapse in H1 FY25.
- Screener shows FY23 PAT ₹2.43 cr vs the restated ₹2.56 cr — cause unknown.

**Half-years (₹ cr)**

| | H2 FY24 | H1 FY25 | H2 FY25 | H1 FY26 | H2 FY26 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Revenue | 11.94 | **3.08** | 17.96 | 20.17 | 20.33 |
| EBITDA margin ex other income | — | — | — | 12.8% | 22.5% |
| Profit before tax | 0.84 | −4.36 | 5.25 | 0.44 | 2.73 |
| Profit after tax | 1.13 | **−4.43** | 5.29 | 0.33 | 2.27 |

- The H1 FY25 loss was an operating collapse: revenue of ₹3.08 cr could not cover fixed costs. The only filed explanation is that a BEML cable-duct supply (₹5.57 cr) "stalled during FY 2024-25 due to a global supply chain crunch"; it restarts from Aug-2026.
- FY25 billing was year-end loaded: receivables jumped to ₹16.53 cr at Mar-25, ₹15.25 cr of it under six months old.

### 3. The branding asset and the rights-issue money — the weak spot
- FY26 intangibles additions: **"Branding" ₹5.73 cr** + models/designs/prototypes ₹0.30 cr. Amortisation on the branding in FY26: ₹5.76 lakh. No goodwill; no acquisition; no subsidiary.
- The rights-issue monitoring agency shows ₹6.14 cr of general-corporate-purpose money spent on "Branding and strategic initiatives".
- The branding spend sits in investing cash flow, which also flatters operating cash flow.

| ₹ cr | FY24 | FY25 | FY26 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Cash from operations | −1.37 | −3.21 | −6.45 |
| Purchase of PPE / intangibles | −1.05 | −4.82 | −7.54 |
| Capital advances | — | −0.27 | −4.48 |
| Free cash flow (CFO − PPE) | −2.42 | −8.03 | −13.99 |

- Counting FY26 capital advances too, free cash flow was about −₹18.5 cr.
- Short-term loans and advances jumped from ₹2.55 cr to ₹19.67 cr, mostly **advances to suppliers ₹17.38 cr** (₹1.02 cr a year earlier); capital advances ₹4.89 cr (₹0.41 cr). Counterparties are not named.

### 4. Future scope
- **Order book:** ₹63.81 cr unexecuted at 31-Dec-2025, then the ₹115.09 cr Titagarh Mumbai Metro contract (6-Feb-2026). Delivering it would roughly triple annual revenue for 2026–2028 — if the company can fund the working capital and execute on time (delivery dates are "tentative").
- **Recent wins:** BEML MRS1 cable-duct restart ₹5.57 cr (from Aug-2026); Titagarh Surat Metro ₹1.03 cr (Aug-2026) and ₹2.63 cr (Sep-2026); Alto-Shaam kitchen parts ₹3.61 cr; BEML high-speed-rail cable ducts ₹0.95 cr.
- **Capacity at IPO (FY23 utilisation):** seats 576 coaches/yr (59%), cable management 576 coaches/yr (15%), grab poles 432 coaches/yr (34%). Utilisation since FY23 is not disclosed; the Peenya plant added space in Nov-2024.
- **Industry:** FY27 railway capex about ₹2.8–2.9 lakh cr (sources differ); rolling-stock line ₹52,109 cr. The company cites ₹29,550 cr of FY26 metro budget support and ~1,095 km of metro/RRTS across 26 cities. No PLI applies.

### Bull case vs bear case
| Bull | Bear |
|---|---|
| ₹115 cr Titagarh contract ≈ 2.8x FY26 revenue; ₹64 cr order book before it | FY26 profit exists only because ₹5.73 cr of "branding" was capitalised |
| Qualified supplier to BEML, Titagarh, CRRC, CAF, Siemens; EN 15085 CL1 welding | Operating cash flow negative three years running; ₹17.4 cr to unnamed suppliers |
| H2 FY26 EBITDA margin back to 22.5% | Extreme customer concentration and lumpy orders (H1 FY25 revenue −78% vs H1 FY24) |
| Market cap only ₹80 cr — about 2x sales vs 3.3–3.9x for the large rolling-stock makers | SEBI/NSE disclosure history; ST-ASM surveillance; no earnings calls or presentations |

ideas.trigger: sme: deep-dive on request — BSE SME medical-device importer/assembler; FY26 revenue +117% on ~₹347 cr of Health Ministry (CMSS) X-ray orders; stock +62% in a month to an all-time high ₹616.20 with no company announcement since 5-Sep-2026
ideas.thesis:
**In plain words.**
- **What it is:** a Mumbai company that imports, assembles and partly makes medical devices — dialysis machines and consumables, IV and infusion sets, X-ray units, nebulisers, oxygen concentrators, eye-care and ECG equipment. It has been Japan's JMS's exclusive India partner for 30+ years.
- **Why sales doubled:** two government orders from the Health Ministry's procurement arm (CMSS) for handheld X-ray machines under the TB-Mukt Bharat programme — ₹82.89 cr (Sep-2025) and ₹264.33 cr (Dec-2025), about ₹347 cr in all. FY26 revenue jumped to ₹231 cr from ₹106.5 cr; profit to ₹18.2 cr from ₹8.1 cr.
- **But the cash did not come in:** operating cash flow was **−₹32 cr** in FY26 as receivables rose by ₹47 cr. Free cash flow has been negative three years running (≈ −₹74 cr in total). The gap was filled by the IPO, a ₹61.5 cr preferential issue and new debt.
- **A related-party deal to question:** in June 2026 it paid ₹20 cr cash for two-thirds of Lifesenz, a tiny loss-making lab (FY25 sales ₹0.57 cr, net worth −₹2.22 cr) whose sellers include the company's own promoters and directors.
- **The price has run far ahead:** at ₹616 it trades at 49x earnings and 38x EV/EBITDA — close to Poly Medicure's P/E, for a mostly-trading business with ~8% net margins and negative cash flow. It is 3.1x the ₹197 price institutions paid a year ago, and the last month's +62% came with no company news.

### 1. What the company is
- BSE SME only: scrip 543916, ISIN INE0GYI01028; listed 5-Jun-2023. Incorporated 1989 (the company says it started in 1985). Registered office Mulund West, Mumbai. 109 permanent employees.
- Promoters: Hanskumar Shamji Shah (MD), Hemant Praful Shah (WTD), Kaushik Hanskumar Shah (WTD & CFO) and four family members. Auditor A D V & Associates (unmodified FY26 opinion, no key audit matters).
- Main partners: JMS Japan/Singapore (49% of revenue in H1 FY26, down from 65% in FY20, per ICRA), Zoncare and SWS (China), Pixxgen and Remedi (Korea), Takagi (Japan), Sonomed (USA). ICRA calls a significant part of revenue "trading" with low value-addition.
- Plants: Achhad/Palghar (dialysis concentrates), Atgaon/Thane (assembly of dialysis machines, nebulisers, oxygen concentrators, dialysers, catheters), Bhiwandi (IV sets; fire on 25-Sep-2024), and a new Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar plant to make JMS Meditape in India. Capacity and utilisation are not disclosed anywhere.
- Subsidiaries: Solar Opto-Medic (Rajkot, 100%, bought for ₹20.25 lakh, Mar-2025) and Lifesenz Cancer Research Labs (66.66%, Jun-2026).
- New tie-ups: Sonomed Escalon (USA) partial-assembly deal for two eye-ultrasound models; GBT Korea C-arm imaging development and supply agreement (sizes undisclosed).

**Revenue by market (₹ cr)**

| | FY24 | FY25 | FY26 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Domestic | 96.17 | 99.00 | 220.41 |
| Exports | 8.70 | 6.34 | 9.88 |
| Export share | 8.3% | 6.0% | 4.3% |

### 2. Growth
| ₹ cr | FY23 | FY24 | FY25 | FY26 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Revenue | 109.15 | 105.61 | 106.53 | **230.99** |
| Gross margin | 26.3% | 26.6% | 29.1% | 23.0% |
| EBITDA ex other income | 10.47 | 10.47 | 9.07 | 23.39 |
| EBITDA margin | 9.6% | 9.9% | 8.5% | 10.1% |
| Other income | 2.35 | 4.31 | 5.11 | 5.73 |
| Profit before tax | 10.06 | 12.78 | 10.56 | 23.63 |
| Profit after tax | 7.64 | 9.80 | 8.13 | **18.23** |

- Revenue was flat for three years (−3.2%, +0.9%) and then jumped +116.8% in FY26 on the CMSS orders. PAT +124%.
- The X-ray orders carry a lower margin: gross margin fell to 21.1% in H2 FY26.
- Other income is about a quarter of FY26 PBT, including a ₹1.46 cr insurance claim and a ₹1.04 cr asset-sale gain.
- Consolidated FY26: revenue ₹231.81 cr, PAT ₹18.19 cr. No dividend since listing.

**Half-years (₹ cr)**

| | H1 FY24 | H2 FY24 | H1 FY25 | H2 FY25 | H1 FY26 | H2 FY26 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Revenue | 47.51 | 58.10 | 48.87 | 57.66 | 64.26 | **166.73** |
| Profit after tax | 3.92 | 5.88 | 3.18 | 4.95 | 5.41 | **12.83** |

### 3. Cash, balance sheet and funding — the weak spot
| ₹ cr | Mar-23 | Mar-24 | Mar-25 | Mar-26 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Net worth | 23.36 | 54.86 | 62.99 | 137.50 |
| Debt | 7.12 | 6.75 | 30.84 | 49.66 |
| Cash & bank | 8.46 | 13.17 | 9.46 | 43.83 |
| Inventory | 14.81 | 21.05 | 42.48 | 58.65 |
| Trade receivables | 17.20 | 21.74 | 20.31 | **67.25** |
| Trade payables | 24.19 | 24.61 | 38.81 | 71.21 |
| Operating cash flow (year) | +6.30 | −7.56 | +8.92 | **−32.02** |
| Free cash flow (year) | +2.4 | −13.1 | −26.4 | −34.2 |

- Mar-26 net worth includes ₹10.34 cr of warrant money. FY25 operating cash flow was later restated to ₹4.59 cr in the FY26 annual report.
- Mar-26 also carries ₹25.94 cr of unsecured "loans from others" at 12%, repayable on demand, from an undisclosed lender; ₹5.28 cr of advances to an unnamed related party; ₹19.03 cr of security deposits; and ₹25.90 cr of tender bank guarantees (contingent).
- Working-capital cycle stretched from 15 days (Mar-23) to 80–87 days (Mar-25/26).
- Returns (our calc): FY26 ROE ≈ 18%, ROCE ≈ 20%.

### 4. Future scope
- **Government demand:** the ₹264.33 cr CMSS order was due by 30-Sep-2026 "subject to negotiations/extension", with commercial terms still under negotiation when announced; the FY26 annual report calls it ~₹350 cr of TB-Mukt Bharat tenders. Repeat orders are not guaranteed — this is one customer, tender-based.
- **Localisation:** JMS Meditape manufacturing in India (new plant), Sonomed eye-ultrasound partial assembly, GBT Korea C-arm — moves from trading toward assembly.
- **Industry:** India's medical-device market is about US$15–16 bn (2025), projected ~US$50 bn by 2030 (company MD&A citing IBEF); 70–80% is imported. The ₹3,420 cr medical-device PLI does not include HSIL as far as found. NPPA caps trade margins at 70% on oxygen concentrators, oximeters, nebulisers and similar products HSIL sells.
- **Credit:** ICRA upgraded bank facilities to BBB (Stable) / A3+ on ₹102.75 cr in Apr-2026 — after an "issuer not cooperating" period in 2023–24.

### Bull case vs bear case
| Bull | Bear |
|---|---|
| ₹347 cr of government X-ray orders doubled revenue in one year | One customer, tender-based; terms were still under negotiation |
| 30-year JMS partnership plus new Korean/US assembly tie-ups | Mostly trading, ~8% net margin, gross margin falling on the X-ray mix |
| Institutions (Singularity funds, Wealthwave) own ~20% after the Sep-2025 issue | Operating cash flow −₹32 cr; ≈ −₹74 cr free cash flow over three years |
| ICRA upgrade to BBB; ROE ≈ 18% | ₹20 cr Lifesenz buy from promoters; undisclosed on-demand lender; 49x P/E after an unexplained +62% month |

ideas.name: Jay Jalaram Technologies Ltd
ideas.trigger: sme: deep-dive on request — NSE Emerge multi-brand phone retail chain (KORE / EROK stores, Gujarat + UP); FY26 revenue +27.6% to ₹852 cr; co-promoter exited 3-Sep-2026 via inter-se transfer; stock +67% in a month after a −40% fall and an NSE price query
ideas.thesis:
**In plain words.**
- **What it is:** an Ahmedabad phone-and-electronics retail chain (KORE and EROK stores; Apple, Samsung, vivo, Oppo, Xiaomi and others; plus TVs and ACs) running company-owned and franchise stores in Gujarat and Uttar Pradesh.
- **Sales grew five-fold in four years:** ₹165 cr (FY22) → ₹852 cr (FY26). Profit ₹8.8 cr in FY26 — a 1.0% margin.
- **But all the profit is brand money.** Brand claims and scheme discounts were ₹37.1 cr in FY26 — 3.2x profit before tax. Without them it would have lost about ₹25 cr before tax. (Same pattern as Umiya Mobile.)
- **Cash has gone out for years:** operating cash flow was negative four years running; FY22–26 cumulative −₹56 cr against +₹24 cr of reported profit. It was funded by ~₹50 cr of new equity and ₹40 cr of franchisee deposits.
- **Governance is in flux:** the co-founder handed his 26.3% stake to the MD and resigned on 3-Sep-2026; the company bought its office from the MD for ₹10 cr; it signed a ₹30 cr loan line to a subsidiary that has never had revenue; the company-secretary post has been vacant since 8-Aug-2026.
- **Price:** ₹180 is 24.9x earnings — about 1.8x Umiya Mobile's multiple for an almost identical business — and still 78% below its 2024 peak of ₹816.

### 1. What the company is
- Listed on NSE Emerge (SME) on 8-Sep-2022; NSE-only; symbol KORE, ISIN INE0J6801010. Incorporated 2012; Ahmedabad.
- Promoters: Kamlesh V. Thakkar (Chairman & MD, now 52.68%), Mukeshkumar Bhatt (8.21%), Vipul Thakkar (8.21%). Co-founder Kamlesh H. Lalwani transferred 26.34% to Thakkar and resigned on 3-Sep-2026 (now 0.09%).
- Auditor V C A N & Co LLP (Ahmedabad) since at least FY19; fee ₹3.0 lakh + ₹0.5 lakh tax audit for an ₹852 cr business; unmodified opinion.
- Honor distribution rights for 7 states (4 years from Jul-2024); B2B share not disclosed. Revolt EV dealership surrendered Nov-2024. No e-commerce revenue disclosed.
- Subsidiary Techgrind Solutions (IT services code, no revenue since 2023; 49% bought from promoter-related holders in May-2026; ₹30 cr loan facility signed 30-Jul-2026).

**Store network**

| Date | Stores | Detail |
|---|---:|---|
| Mar-2024 deck | 220 | 44 company-owned, 175 franchise, 8 warehouses; Gujarat 100 (39 cities), UP 73 (26 cities) |
| May-2025 deck | 180+ | fall from 220 not explained |
| FY26 annual report | 180+ | same wording as FY25 — current count effectively unknown |

- Three formats: company-owned; franchisee-owned but company-operated; franchisee-owned and operated. The company appears to own the stock at franchise stores, book the sale and pay a commission (our inference).
- Company-stated store economics (Mar-2024): ~600 sq ft, ~₹39 lakh capex per store incl. stock. Revenue per store ≈ ₹4.7 cr a year (₹852 cr ÷ ~180; store count uncertain).

### 2. Growth — and where the profit comes from
| ₹ cr | FY22 | FY23 | FY24 | FY25 | FY26 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Revenue from operations | 165.26 | 249.20 | 538.72 | 667.68 | **851.80** |
| Growth | — | 50.8% | 116.2% | 23.9% | 27.6% |
| of which brand claim income | 5.08 | 12.59 | 20.62 | 36.90 | 29.55 |
| Scheme discount netted in purchases | 8.37 | 4.78 | 7.96 | 9.35 | 7.59 |
| Franchise commission paid | 4.48 | 6.83 | 12.73 | 13.35 | 19.98 |
| EBITDA | 2.59 | 4.69 | 9.84 | 13.03 | 15.52 |
| Profit before tax | 1.14 | 3.64 | 6.32 | 9.06 | 11.74 |
| Profit after tax | 0.85 | 2.51 | 4.86 | 6.76 | **8.77** |
| **Claims + discount ÷ PBT** | 11.8x | 4.8x | 4.5x | 5.1x | **3.2x** |

| Margin | FY22 | FY23 | FY24 | FY25 | FY26 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Gross margin | 9.73% | 10.95% | 9.10% | 8.32% | 7.29% |
| Merchandise margin before claims & discount | 1.2% | 3.8% | 3.6% | 1.2% | 2.7% |
| EBITDA margin | 1.6% | 1.9% | 1.8% | 2.0% | 1.8% |
| PAT margin | 0.5% | 1.0% | 0.9% | 1.0% | 1.03% |

- Brand "claim income" sits inside revenue; "scheme discount" is deducted from purchases; incentives are recognised "based on eligibility". Claims receivable ₹9.44 cr at Mar-26.
- Claim income fell 20% in FY26 while sales rose 28%.
- Consolidated FY26 PAT ₹10.28 cr includes a one-off ₹1.73 cr gain (sale of Hear More Techlife) booked in other income, not exceptional items.

**Half-years (standalone, ₹ cr)**

| | H1 FY24 | H2 FY24 | H1 FY25 | H2 FY25 | H1 FY26 | H2 FY26 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Revenue | 216.06 | 322.66 | 328.59 | 339.09 | 356.95 | **494.85** |
| Profit after tax | 0.65 | 4.21 | 3.35 | 3.41 | 3.66 | 5.11 |

- H2 FY26 revenue +46% year on year.

### 3. Cash and balance sheet — the weak spot
| ₹ cr, 31-Mar | FY22 | FY23 | FY24 | FY25 | FY26 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Inventory | 18.4 | 39.2 | 90.6 | 88.3 | 109.6 |
| Receivables | 2.7 | 3.1 | 9.3 | 7.6 | 14.8 |
| Payables | 17.4 | 17.7 | 27.5 | 22.3 | 31.5 |
| Borrowings | 10.7 | 19.8 | 46.1 | 55.7 | 40.9 |
| Franchisee deposits | 8.9 | 16.0 | 30.4 | 32.8 | 40.0 |
| Net worth | 10.7 | 23.6 | 28.5 | 67.5 | 83.7 |
| Operating cash flow | −6.49 | −11.81 | −25.25 | −33.19 | +20.40 |
| Capex | 0.16 | 1.40 | 2.76 | 1.53 | 11.96 |

- FY26's positive operating cash flow rests on a ₹16.1 cr fall in loans and advances and ₹7.2 cr of new franchisee deposits; without those it would be about −₹2.9 cr (agent's arithmetic).
- Advances to suppliers jumped from ₹4.35 cr to **₹38.03 cr** in FY25, right after the ₹29.7 cr preferential raise; ₹20.09 cr at Mar-26, of which ₹10.59 cr more than a year old and not provided for.
- FY26 capex includes **₹10 cr to buy the registered office from the MD** (related party).
- Related-party sales to Jay Jalaram Enterprise (a director's firm): ₹7.46 cr in FY26.
- FY22 GST demands (₹1.67 cr + ₹0.32 cr show-cause) disclosed but not counted as contingent liabilities.

### 4. Future scope
- Franchise-led expansion across Gujarat, UP, Delhi, Haryana, Rajasthan, Maharashtra, Chhattisgarh and Punjab; employee cost and rent fell in FY26 as commission rose — the shift to franchise is underway.
- Main-board migration approved by postal ballot (8-May-2026); application not yet made.
- **Industry:** 2025 was good for offline chains — India shipped 152 million phones (+0.5%), average price a record $282, offline share up to 57%, Apple a record 14 million units (IDC). 2026 is turning: Q2 shipments −10%, sub-₹15k phones −45%, memory costs up ~4x since Sep-2025, full-year forecast −13% (Counterpoint). Financing is over half of mainline sales.
- Because profit equals brand incentives, a shrinking market that squeezes brand incentive budgets is the key threat for 2026–27.

### Bull case vs bear case
| Bull | Bear |
|---|---|
| Five-fold revenue growth FY22→FY26; H2 FY26 +46% | Profit is 3.2x smaller than the brand money it depends on |
| Offline share of Indian phone sales rising; premium/Apple mix growing | Four years of negative operating cash flow (−₹56 cr cumulative) |
| Franchise model cuts rent and staff cost | Co-founder exit, ₹10 cr office bought from the MD, ₹30 cr line to a no-revenue subsidiary |
| Main-board migration approved | 24.9x P/E vs Umiya 13.5x for the same business; memory-cost slump in 2026 |

ideas.name: Fonebox Retail Ltd
ideas.trigger: sme: deep-dive on request — NSE Emerge phone retail chain (294 stores, Gujarat + Maharashtra); FY26 revenue +56% to ₹535 cr; stock +85% in a month on mostly circuit-limited sessions after 30 lakh shares were issued at ₹85.80 to buy NWOM Retailers
ideas.thesis:
**In plain words.**
- **What it is:** an Ahmedabad phone retail chain (Fonebox, Fonebook, My Mobile, Fone Point stores) selling Apple, Samsung, vivo, Oppo, Realme, Xiaomi and others — 33 company-owned stores and 261 franchise stores across Gujarat and Maharashtra at March 2026.
- **Growth:** FY26 revenue ₹535 cr (+56%), profit ₹6.8 cr (+50%) — a 1.3% margin. Growth has been steady since its 2024 IPO.
- **Cleaner than its peers on one point:** brand rebates are booked inside cost of goods, not as other income, and the IPO money sits in financing cash flow. But the rebate amount is not disclosed, so how much of the profit is brand money cannot be measured.
- **Cash depends on franchisee deposits:** franchisees have put in ₹48.9 cr of security deposits — more than the company's net worth of ₹41.3 cr. Take the deposit inflows out and operating cash flow was negative in each of FY24, FY25 and FY26 (≈ −₹6 to −₹8 cr a year).
- **Related-party dealings are large:** ≈ ₹91 cr of FY26 purchases (≈18%) came from promoter-linked distributors; shareholders approved FY27 limits up to ₹450 cr, including a new firm run by the Chairman's son. The Sep-2026 purchase of NWOM Retailers was a share swap with people who became promoters on allotment.
- **Price:** +85% in a month with no new results; now in trade-for-trade. At ₹167.65 it is about 2x the ₹85.80 swap price and 32.7x post-issue earnings — 2.4x Umiya Mobile's multiple.

### 1. What the company is
- Listed on NSE Emerge (SME) on 2-Feb-2024; NSE-only; symbol FONEBOX, ISIN INE0Q4701019. Incorporated 2021 in Ahmedabad; built by buying store chains (11 My Mobile stores in Surat, 37 HK Retail stores in Ahmedabad, Safe Zone Mobile, iMagic Mobile).
- Promoters (18-Sep-2026): Manishbhai G. Patel (Chairman) 13.86%, Parth L. Desai (ED & CFO) 9.33%, Jigar L. Desai 9.33%, Dhrumil P. Shah 7.55% and Pankaj K. Vasudeva 7.54% (both new via the NWOM swap), Amitkumar G. Patel (MD) 2.08%; 21 promoter-group holders in all.
- Auditor R K Kotadiya & Co LLP (no change since listing; re-appointed FY26–FY30). Samsung "Organized Trade Partner" since Jul-2025.
- Zero-cost EMI through Bajaj Finance, HDFC, ICICI, IDFC First, HDB and others; card/bank charges were ₹4.85 cr in FY25 (1.4% of revenue). EMI share of sales not disclosed. No e-commerce.
- New: 100% of NWOM Retailers (share swap, Sep-2026) and 5% of Digiwave Global Trading FZCO, Dubai (AED 10,000, Mar-2026; promoter-group persons also invested).

**Stores**

| Date | Company-owned | Franchise | Total | Source |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| Jul-2024 | — | — | 181 | announcement (all Gujarat) |
| 31-Mar-2025 | 33 | 162 | 195 | FY25 annual report |
| 31-Jan-2026 | — | — | 251+ | announcement |
| 31-Mar-2026 | 33 | 261 | 294 | FY26 annual report (Gujarat + Maharashtra) |
| 29-Apr-2026 | — | — | 275+ | announcement — conflicts with 294 a month earlier |

- The franchise model is described two ways: the annual report says the company earns "1% of turnover"; the Nov-2024 call said franchise stores are "franchisee owned, but the operation under Fonebox management". The accounts fit the second: franchise sales appear to be booked as company revenue, with commission paid out (₹9.98 cr in FY25).
- Derived store economics (FY26): ≈ ₹2.19 cr revenue and ≈ ₹2.8 lakh profit per average store; ≈ ₹18–19 lakh deposit per franchise store.
- Expansion announced: ~10 stores in Madhya Pradesh (Jan-2026), 25 in Punjab, Himachal Pradesh and Haryana (Jul-2026).

### 2. Growth
| ₹ cr | FY23 | FY24 | FY25 | FY26 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Revenue | 196.26 | 297.61 | 342.73 | **535.08** |
| Growth | — | +51.6% | +15.2% | +56.1% |
| Gross profit | 19.57 | 28.83 | 34.37 | 57.79 |
| Gross margin | 9.97% | 9.69% | 10.03% | 10.80% |
| EBITDA | 3.90 | 6.12 | 7.39 | 10.82 |
| EBITDA margin | 1.99% | 2.06% | 2.16% | 2.02% |
| Profit after tax | 1.60 | 3.43 | 4.55 | **6.80** |
| PAT growth | — | +115% | +32% | +50% |

**Half-years (₹ cr)**

| | H1 FY25 | H2 FY25 | H1 FY26 | H2 FY26 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Revenue | 164.65 | 178.08 | 223.72 | **311.36** |
| Gross margin | — | — | 9.77% | 11.54% |
| EBITDA | — | — | 3.76 | 7.07 |
| Profit after tax | 1.72 | 2.83 | 2.28 | **4.53** |

- Product mix FY26: mobiles and accessories ₹521.63 cr, consumer durables ₹12.02 cr.
- **Where the brand money sits:** the policy nets rebates and discounts into inventory cost; other income is ≈ zero every year. So incentives are inside the 10.8% gross margin, not added below it as at Umiya. The annual amount is not disclosed (FY26 notes are image-only). Size marker: "scheme incentive receivable" was ₹5.97 cr at Mar-25 — 131% of FY25 profit.
- Guidance track record: the Nov-2024 call guided FY25 "400 plus" (actual ₹342.7 cr) and "around 700 crores with PAT of at least 8 crore" (year unclear; FY26 was ₹535 cr / ₹6.8 cr).

### 3. Cash and balance sheet — the weak spot
| ₹ cr | Mar-24 | Mar-25 | Sep-25 | Mar-26 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Net worth | 29.95 | 34.50 | 36.77 | 41.30 |
| Franchise security deposits | 17.80 | 29.69 | 38.77 | **48.91** |
| Short-term borrowings | 0.15 | 3.31 | 6.49 | 0.00 |
| Trade payables | 10.55 | 13.79 | 28.72 | 31.43 |
| Inventory | 29.70 | 38.65 | 56.51 | 72.12 |
| Receivables | 1.43 | 2.46 | 0.78 | 2.11 |
| Cash + bank | 13.68 | 22.11 | 30.29 | 28.51 |

| ₹ cr | FY23 | FY24 | FY25 | FY26 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Operating cash flow (reported) | −2.08 | −0.16 | +6.13 | +11.20 |
| Franchise deposits inside it | — | +6.18 | +11.89 | ≈ +19.21 |
| Operating cash flow ex deposits | — | ≈ −6.3 | ≈ −5.8 | ≈ −8.0 |
| Capex | 1.18 | 0.44 | 0.45 | 0.94 |

- Inventory grew 87% in FY26 vs revenue +56%; inventory days 40 → 46 → 55.
- No IPO premium inside operating cash flow; no debt to speak of; no contingent liabilities (FY25).

### 4. Future scope
- More stores (north India, Madhya Pradesh) and the NWOM acquisition: NWOM turnover ₹130.09 cr (FY24) → ₹253.21 cr (FY25); its profit is undisclosed. H1 FY27 will be the first period with NWOM consolidated.
- **Industry:** 2025 favoured offline chains — India shipped 152 million phones (+0.5%), offline share up to 57%, average price +8% (IDC). 2026 is turning: Q2 shipments −10%, sub-₹15k −45%, memory prices up ~4x since Sep-2025, full-year forecast −13% (Counterpoint). EMI finances over half of offline sales.
- Higher prices help revenue per phone and EMI-led stores; falling budget volumes and brand incentive cuts hit 1–2% margin retailers directly.

### Bull case vs bear case
| Bull | Bear |
|---|---|
| Revenue +56% in FY26; H2 FY26 PAT +60% | 1.3% net margin; rebate size undisclosed |
| Rebates in cost of goods, IPO money in financing — cleaner books than Umiya | Operating cash flow negative every year once franchise deposits are removed |
| No debt; ₹28.5 cr cash | ₹48.9 cr of franchisee deposits exceed net worth |
| Store count 195 → 294 in a year; NWOM adds ≈ ₹250 cr of turnover | Heavy related-party purchases; NWOM swap with incoming promoters; 32.7x P/E after +85% month |

ideas.name: Utssav CZ Gold Jewels Ltd
ideas.trigger: sme: deep-dive on request — NSE Emerge B2B maker of lightweight CZ gold jewellery; FY26 revenue +78.7% / PAT +136%, but volume grew only ~11–19%; stock at an all-time high ₹722.10 (+296% in a year) after an NSE price-movement query on 17-Sep-2026
ideas.thesis:
**In plain words.**
- **What it is:** a Mumbai workshop that makes lightweight 18K/20K/22K gold jewellery set with cubic zirconia (CZ) — about 10 grams a piece — and sells it only to other businesses: big jewellers like Kalyan, Lalithaa, TBZ and Joyalukkas (~30% of sales) and distributors and small retailers (~70%). It is now adding plain gold and diamond pieces.
- **Headline growth looks huge:** FY26 revenue ₹1,155 cr (+79%), profit ₹59 cr (+136%).
- **But most of it is the gold price, not more jewellery.** Kilograms sold grew only about 11% (company) or 19% (CARE Ratings); the price of each kilo rose 50–61%. Gold itself rose ~59% on MCX over the year.
- **Cash goes out, borrowed money comes in:** operating cash flow was −₹89 cr in FY25 and −₹61 cr in FY26. Borrowings went from ₹73 cr to ₹186 cr in two years; its bank lines are ~96% used.
- **Unhedged gold:** about 150 kg (₹158 cr) of stock is not hedged — a 10% fall in gold would cost about ₹16 cr, roughly a quarter of FY26 profit.
- **Same owners as Shanti Gold:** the promoters also control listed Shanti Gold International, which guaranteed Utssav's bank loans; the MD denied promoter loans on a call while the filings showed ₹2.8 cr owed to him.
- **Price:** ₹722 is an all-time high, +296% in a year and 4x in six months; NSE queried the move on 17-Sep. 30.6x earnings — about twice Shanti Gold's 16.0x (restated trailing).

### 1. What the company is
- Incorporated 2007; listed on NSE Emerge (SME) on 7-Aug-2024; NSE-only; symbol UTSSAV, ISIN INE06IJ01010.
- One site: Andheri (E), Mumbai, 8,275 sq ft (corporate office + 2 production units), adding ~5,600 sq ft. About 130 staff (employee cost only ₹4.35 cr, 0.38% of sales).
- Promoters (Jagawat family): Pankajkumar H. Jagawat (MD, 62.2% after warrant conversion), Shashank B. Jagawat (WTD), Rakesh S. Jagawat (CFO); promoter group includes Shanti Gold International, Uzuri Jewels, Ganesh Gold, Sanskriti Gold, Shanti Developers.
- Auditor Jain V. & Co. (unmodified opinions FY24–FY26; no change). CEO Harpreet Singh Guleria since Apr-2024.
- Reach: 23 states + 2 UTs, 430+ touch points, 112 new clients in FY26. Exports ~1% of FY26 sales (UAE hub).
- New: Indian subsidiary Utssav Gold and Diamond (Jul-2026); a UAE subsidiary approved Feb-2026 (incorporation not confirmed).

**Capacity — stated four different ways**

| Source | Installed capacity | Utilisation |
|---|---:|---:|
| IPO documents / CARE Sep-2025 | 1,500 kg/yr | — |
| May-2026 presentation (p.4–5) | 2,000 kg | ~65% (FY26) |
| May-2026 presentation (p.10) | 1,500 kg | — |
| MD on May-2026 call | 2,500 kg | ~65% (up to 90% in season) |

- Target 6–7 tonnes a year through new buildings; FY27 capex ≈ ₹50 cr.

### 2. Growth — gold price vs kilograms
| ₹ cr | FY24 | FY25 | FY26 |

ideas.thesis:
**In plain words.**
- **What it is:** a Mumbai company (since 2003) that makes 22-carat gold jewellery set with cubic zirconia — bangles, rings, necklaces, bridal sets — and sells it only to jewellers and wholesalers (Joyalukkas, Lalithaa, Alukkas, Kalyan and 400+ others). Listed on the main board (NSE + BSE) in Aug-2025.
- **Headline growth:** FY26 revenue ₹2,019 cr (+82%), profit ₹140 cr (+159%). But kilograms sold grew only ~15% (1,518 → 1,748 kg); the rest is the gold price, which rose ~58% in rupees. Revenue per gram tracks the gold price almost one for one.
- **Profit was helped by holding unhedged gold while prices rose.** Management's own "core" margin is 3.5–4% PAT; FY26 was 6.9%. On that core margin, roughly 40–50% of FY26 profit came from gold-price gains (our arithmetic).
- **The accounts changed mid-stream:** in May-2026 it switched inventory costing from FIFO to weighted-average, restated back to Apr-2024. FY26 profit on the new method is ₹140 cr; on the old method it would have been ₹193 cr. Quarterly figures published earlier were restated (Q2 FY26 PAT ₹43.8 cr → ₹26.0 cr).
- **Cash goes out fast:** operating cash flow −₹261 cr in FY26. It raised ₹360 cr in the Aug-2025 IPO and another ₹100 cr in an Aug-2026 rights issue (promoters did not subscribe), and is seeking a ₹2,000 cr borrowing limit.
- **Governance points:** the same promoters control listed rival Utssav CZ Gold Jewels (a promoter sits on its board and it guaranteed Utssav's bank loans); surplus cash went into listed shares, including a customer (Lalithaa) and a steel company (Ratnaveer).
- **Price:** ₹325.68 is an all-time high after +30% in a week on HFT-dominated volume with only 9% delivery and no company news. 16x trailing (restated) earnings — cheaper than Utssav (30.6x) but the gold-gain share of profit matters.

### 1. What the company is
- Main board, listed 01-Aug-2025 on NSE (SHANTIGOLD) and BSE (544459); ISIN INE06ZD01017. Partnership from 2003; public limited company since 2013.
- Promoters: Pankajkumar H. Jagawat (Chairman & MD), Manojkumar N. Jain (WTD), Shashank B. Jagawat (non-executive; also a whole-time director of Utssav CZ Gold Jewels). Auditor J. Kala & Associates (no change). CARE A- (Stable) / A2+ (Jan-2026). 286 employees.
- Subsidiary: Shanti Gold Jewellery Trading LLC, Dubai (incorporated May-2026; awaiting RBI approval; no operations to Jun-2026).
- New lines: machine-made plain gold, Mangalsutra, Turkish jewellery, Cuban bracelets.

**FY26 revenue by purity (₹ cr)**

| Purity | FY26 | Share |
|---|---:|---:|
| 22KT | 1,871.3 | 92.7% |
| 18KT | 85.4 | 4.2% |
| 24KT | 50.4 | 2.5% |
| Other | 11.2 | 0.6% |

**Customer concentration (share of revenue)**

| Top 1 | 8.92% | 7.32% | 7.98% |
| Top 5 | 24.14% | 23.29% | 30.46% |
| Top 10 | 36.43% | 34.49% | **44.82%** |

- South India fell from 72.8% of revenue (FY25) to 44.6% (FY26); the ~₹1,036 cr sold elsewhere has no state split disclosed. Exports ₹82.9 cr (4.1%).

**Capacity**

| Plant | Capacity (kg/yr) | Status |
|---|---:|---|
| Andheri, Mumbai | 2,700 | running (68% in Jan-2026) |
| Marol, Mumbai | 4,000 | production from 08-Jun-2026 (₹8.5 cr capex) |
| Jaipur (plain gold) | 1,200 | under construction; now expected Nov–Dec 2026 (delayed) |
| **Total planned** | **7,900** | |

- FY26 sold 1,747.8 kg (≈65% of 2,700 kg). FY27 guidance of +30–40% volume would use only ~34–37% of the 6,700 kg running base (our arithmetic).

### 2. Growth — kilograms vs gold price
| ₹ cr | FY23 | FY24 | FY25 (restated) | FY26 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Revenue | 679.4 | 711.4 | 1,106.4 | **2,018.7** |
| EBITDA | 42.7 | 49.9 | 89.9 | 199.0 |
| EBITDA margin | 6.3% | 7.0% | 8.1% | 9.9% |
| Profit after tax | 19.8 | 26.9 | 54.1 | **140.15** |
| PAT margin | 2.9% | 3.8% | 4.9% | 6.9% |

| | FY25 | FY26 | Change |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Kilograms sold | 1,517.5 | 1,747.8 | +15.2% |
| Revenue per gram | ₹7,291 | ₹11,550 | +58.4% |
| International gold, ₹ per 10 g (avg) | 71,836 | 113,813 | +58.4% |

- FY26 growth ≈ +15% volume × +58% price. Revenue per gram tracks the 24K international gold price at 0.975–1.008x each quarter (our derivation).

**Quarters (₹ cr; FY26 restated to weighted-average cost)**

| | Q1 FY26 | Q2 FY26 | Q3 FY26 | Q4 FY26 | Q1 FY27 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Revenue | 292.78 | 430.08 | 636.92 | 658.93 | **716.38** |
| Kilograms | 323 | 427 | 535 | 463 | 522.1 |
| Profit after tax | 34.36 | 26.00 | 27.87 (derived) | 51.93 | **50.48** |
| PAT as first published (FIFO) | 24.64 | 43.82 | — | — | — |

- Q1 FY27: revenue +144.7%, volume +61.6%, PAT +46.9% y/y; EBITDA margin 9.97%, of which management attributes 2–2.5 points to inventory gains.

### 3. Cash and balance sheet — the weak spot
| ₹ cr, 31-Mar | FY25 | FY26 |
|---|---:|---:|
| Inventory | 133.9 | 347.5 |
| Receivables | 181.6 | 362.9 |
| Borrowings | 233.0 | 205.6 |
| Cash + other bank balances | — | 49.2 |
| Net worth | 137.7 | 598.4 |
| Operating cash flow | −15.3 | **−260.6** |
| Capex | — | 6.3 |

- Inventory days 65 → 49 → 70 and receivable days 40 → 60 → 66 (FY24→FY26, year-end). No expected-credit-loss provision on ₹363 cr of receivables. Finished goods ₹320 cr but work-in-progress nil — unusual for a manufacturer.
- FY26 cash flow appears to add interest and rent income inside operating cash flow and deduct them again in investing (FY25 was presented correctly); corrected CFO ≈ −₹272 cr (our arithmetic).
- Working-capital gap ₹742 cr in FY26, projected ₹1,159 cr for FY27 (rights letter of offer). Borrowing limit being raised to ₹2,000 cr (AGM 28-Sep-2026).

### 4. Future scope
- Guidance: FY27 revenue ≈ ₹3,500 cr, volume +30–40%, core EBITDA margin 7.5–8% and core PAT 3.5–4%. Marol (+4,000 kg) is running; Jaipur plain gold due Nov–Dec 2026; Dubai trading arm pending RBI approval.
- **Industry:** Indian jewellery tonnage is falling (Q1 2026 −19%, Q2 −15%) while value rises (Q1 +47%). Buyers shift to lighter, lower-carat and studded pieces (good for CZ). Import duty rose from 6% to 15% on 13-May-2026; WGC expects 2026 demand −50–60 t (~10%). Organised share projected to rise from 35% (CY23) to ~60% by CY29; HUID hallmarking now covers 392 districts.

### Bull case vs bear case
| Bull | Bear |
|---|---|
| Real volume growth (+15% FY26, +62% Q1 FY27) with new Marol capacity | Most of FY26's growth and much of its margin came from the gold price |
| 400+ organised-jeweller customers; organised share rising | Accounting method changed and quarters restated; a cash-flow sign error |
| 16x trailing earnings, below Utssav (30.6x) and Sky Gold (36.7x) | Operating cash flow −₹261 cr; two equity raises in 13 months; ₹2,000 cr borrowing limit |
| ROE 38%, CARE A- | Common promoters with rival Utssav; cash put into a customer's and a steel company's shares; HFT-driven all-time high |

ideas.valuepickr:
**What ValuePickr is saying**
There is one young dedicated thread, "Shanti Gold- Sky Gold in making?", started on 30-Aug-2026: 6 posts, last post 28-Sep-2026, about 1,100 views. The opening post by Chandan_Sharma is a long, balanced write-up (business, promoters, Q1 FY27 call, risks) with a disclosed small holding. The same author posted a shorter version in his own journal thread. Replies are brief. They note that a key customer (Lalithaa) got only a token investment, and they ask why Shanti Gold and Utssav CZ share promoters and why Shanti Gold bought Ratnaveer shares (unanswered). The main debate is fast growth and capacity additions against cash-hungry working capital and the overlap with the sister company Utssav. Nobody on the forum discusses the May-2026 FIFO-to-weighted-average restatement.

But the same person (DIN 01843846), Pankajkumar Jagawat, is Managing Director of Utssav and Chairman & MD of Shanti Gold. - The promoters have no criminal cases against them — Chandan_Sharma — says he searched; no primary document reviewed this run covers it.

ideas.trigger: sme: deep-dive on request — BSE SME maker of air-conditioning and refrigeration systems for Indian Navy and Coast Guard ships; FY26 revenue +55.5% / PAT +65.6%; CARE upgrade to BBB- on 15-Sep-2026; stock +127% in six months to ₹407.60
ideas.thesis:
**In plain words.**
- **What it is:** a Karad (Maharashtra) company that designs and builds air-conditioning plants, refrigeration plants, chillers, air handlers and control panels for warships and Coast Guard vessels. Its customers are the Navy's shipyards and depots — Mazagon Dock, Garden Reach, Goa Shipyard, Hindustan Shipyard, Cochin Shipyard, Naval Dockyard Mumbai. It claims about 64% of naval HVAC&R.
- **Growth:** FY26 revenue ₹153.6 cr (+56%), profit ₹21.5 cr (+66%). Revenue has compounded about 45% a year since FY23.
- **But the order book is shrinking:** ₹327.6 cr at Sep-2025 → ₹270.8 cr at Mar-2026 (₹279.7 cr at Jun-2026, per CARE). Orders announced since April 2026 add up to only about ₹21 cr, against management's promise of ~40% annual growth.
- **Cash is slow:** the Navy's shipyards pay only after installation, so money is tied up for about a year (cash conversion ~368 days). Free cash flow was negative for three years running (FY26 −₹10.5 cr).
- **Governance points to check:** IPO spending rules widened the day before listing (to include residential property); 15% of the fresh issue went on issue costs; four family members on the board; ESOP shares issued at ₹2 face value; the cash-flow filing was revised twice.
- **Price:** ₹407.60 is 68x FY26 profit and 44x EBITDA — priced like a large defence stock for a ₹154 cr, one-customer-type business. An early backer (Maharashtra Defence & Aerospace Venture Fund) keeps selling.

### 1. What the company is
- BSE SME only (listed 01-Aug-2025): scrip 544458, symbol SHREEREF, ISIN INE0FMZ01045, face value ₹2. Registered office Karad, Satara.
- Products: AC plants 5–300 TR (including oil-free magnetic-bearing chillers), refrigeration plants 0.5–35 TR, self-contained and split ACs, air-handling and fan-coil units, turnkey ship HVAC&R, motor starter and control panels, heat exchangers, spares and service. Navy approvals from DME, DNA and DEE.
- Programmes cited (company claims): P17A Nilgiri frigates, P75 Scorpene AC indigenisation, Fleet Support Ships at HSL, Coast Guard FPVs at GSL and MDL, NGMV at CSL, NGOPV.
- Promoters: Ravalnath G. Shende (CMD, 35.0%), Rajashree R. Shende (ED, 9.56%), Devashree Nampurkar (WTD); Rucha R. Shende joined the board Feb-2026 — four family directors. CEO Abhijit Saoji; CFO Manoj Kothale. 152 permanent employees.
- Auditor SSSS & Associates, Karad (unmodified opinion; ₹11 lakh fee). Its partner shares a surname with the company secretary who resigned in Jan-2026 — any relationship is unknown.
- Subsidiaries: Trezor Technologies (no revenue; holds the Smardt data-centre chiller distribution deal; lends ₹2 cr to the parent) and Aquilon Deep Chill (approved Aug-2026). Danfoss Turbocor service partner since Mar-2026.

**FY26 closing order book by product (₹ cr)**

| HVAC | 159.69 | 59.0% |
| AC plant | 61.66 | 22.8% |
| Refrigeration plant | 17.99 | 6.6% |

| Date | Order book (₹ cr) | Source |

### 2. Growth
| ₹ cr | FY23 | FY24 | FY25 | FY26 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Revenue | 50.58 | 80.31 | 98.73 | **153.55** |
| Growth | — | +58.8% | +22.9% | +55.5% |
| Gross margin | — | 50.1% | 49.3% | 43.6% |
| EBITDA (ex other income) | 11.90 | 24.15 | 26.95 | 32.81 |
| EBITDA margin | 23.5% | 30.1% | 27.3% | **21.4%** |
| Profit after tax | 3.38 | 11.03 | 13.00 | **21.53** |

- Margins are falling as the high-margin spares share dropped from ~30% of revenue (FY25) to ~7% (FY26); management targets 15–20% spares and a 20–24% EBITDA margin.
- FY26 tax was only 13.8% of profit before tax.
- Restated FY25 in the prospectus (revenue ₹99.10 cr, PAT ₹13.55 cr) differs from the audited FY25 (₹98.73 cr, ₹13.00 cr).

| | H1 FY26 | H2 FY26 |
|---|---:|---:|
| Revenue | 50.39 | **103.16** |
| EBITDA margin | 11.2% | 26.3% |
| Profit after tax | 1.57 | **19.96** |
| PAT margin | 3.1% | 19.3% |

- The business is heavily second-half: H2 carried 93% of FY26 profit.

### 3. Cash and balance sheet — the weak spot
| ₹ cr | Mar-25 | Sep-25 | Mar-26 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Net worth | 118.2 | 196.19 | 215.86 |
| Receivables | 95.16 | 64.28 | 105.43 |
| Inventory | 47.40 | 49.58 | 54.77 |
| Payables | 17.06 | 8.61 | 27.02 |
| Borrowings | 46.9 | 24.19 | 37.46 |
| Cash | 5.93 | 17.08 | 57.66 |
| Current investments (FDs + MFs) | 3.50 | 50.01 | 5.15 |
| Capital work in progress | 0.06 | 0.14 | 17.55 |

| ₹ cr (standalone) | FY24 | FY25 | FY26 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Operating cash flow | −5.33 | −24.92 | +13.85 |
| Capex | 1.43 | 13.51 | 24.38 |
| Free cash flow | −6.76 | −38.43 | **−10.53** |

- FY26 working capital (days): receivables 251, inventory 231, payables 114 → cash conversion ≈ 368 days (FY25 higher). Invoices are raised only after installation in the shipbuilding process (CARE).
- Bank guarantees jumped to ₹28.10 cr from ₹9.66 cr. Non-current investments include commercial property ₹2.10 cr and **residential property ₹2.50 cr**; one building is still titled in the CMD's name.

### 4. Future scope
- **Navy build-out:** ~45 major platforms under construction; 75 ships on order (May-2026); a 200-ship fleet targeted by 2035; 19 commissionings planned in 2026. The company cites ~₹2.35 lakh cr of approvals with HVAC&R at ~1% of project value and expects ~₹1,000 cr of naval HVAC tenders in FY27 (company figures, not verified).
- **Capacity:** new Unit 2 at Hanbarwadi, Satara (50,000 sq ft on 6.5 acres, expandable to 100,000) inaugurated 20-Jun-2026; Phase-1 capex ~₹25 cr, possibly 40–50% subsidised under Maharashtra's PSI scheme (company claim). Management says current facilities can support ~₹400 cr of revenue.
- **New adjacencies:** data-centre cooling via Smardt oil-free chillers (reference site targeted FY27, meaningful revenue FY28); Danfoss Turbocor service aftermarket.
- **Guidance:** ~40% revenue CAGR for 3–5 years; an earlier deck targeted ₹1,000 cr sales and ₹120–130 cr PAT by FY30–31.

| Bull | Bear |
|---|---|
| Dominant niche (claims ~64% of naval HVAC&R) with Navy type approvals | Order book down 17% from its Sep-2025 peak; only ~₹21 cr of new orders announced since April |
| Navy's 200-ship plan and indigenisation lists | ~368-day cash cycle; free cash flow negative three years running |
| Revenue CAGR ~45% since FY23; CARE upgrade to BBB- | EBITDA margin falling (30% → 21%) as spares shrink |
| New plant, data-centre chiller option | 68x P/E, 44x EV/EBITDA; IPO-proceeds and filing-quality flags; family board; early investor selling |

### Claims on the forum not verified
- Prospectus risk factors: late GST, income-tax and PF filings, and no price-variation clause in contracts — Naresh. The prospectus was not read. In the H1 call an analyst said bids usually carry an escalation clause, and management's answer did not settle the point.

- A ₹90,000 cr German submarine deal will bring follow-on orders — ADI129. This is speculation.

### Where the forum disagrees with the filings

ideas.name: Ratnaveer Precision Engineering Ltd
ideas.trigger: deep-dive on request — main-board stainless-steel sheets, washers and pipes maker adding a ₹338–472 cr copper-clad-laminate plant; seven equity raises (~₹815 cr) in three years; ₹330 cr rights issue allotted 10-Sep-2026; stock at an all-time high ₹333.95 (+145% in six months); Shanti Gold bought 2.65 lakh shares on 25-Sep
ideas.thesis:
**In plain words.**
- **What it is:** a Vadodara company (since 2002) that processes stainless steel into finishing sheets (about half of sales), washers and small stamped parts (including solar-roof hooks), welded and seamless pipes, and nuts and bolts. It is now building a plant to make copper-clad laminates — the base board for printed circuit boards — with government ECMS support.
- **Growth is steady, not spectacular:** revenue ₹1,069 cr in FY26 (+20%), profit ₹64 cr (+37%); about 30% a year since FY23. EBITDA margin ~10.5%. Q1 FY27: revenue +19%, profit +22%.
- **But it keeps raising money:** seven equity raises in three years — IPO, preferential shares, promoter warrants twice, convertible preference shares, a ₹185 cr QIP and a ₹330 cr rights issue — about ₹815 cr in all. Share count up 72% since the IPO. Yet at 30-Jun-2026, ₹150 cr of QIP money was still sitting in fixed deposits pledged against its own overdraft.
- **Cash goes out:** free cash flow was negative three years running (≈ −₹260 cr). In FY26 receivables more than doubled and advances to suppliers tripled (to ₹170 cr).
- **The export story doesn't match the accounts:** investor decks call it the "#1 exporter of SS washers" with 35–52% exports; the audited accounts show exports of only 5.2% of FY26 revenue.
- **Promoter:** stake down from 55.5% to 38.7%; he skipped the ₹264 rights issue but holds 38 lakh warrants at ₹159.25 — about 110% in the money.
- **Price:** ₹333.95 is an all-time high, +145% in six months, on very heavy trading (August turnover ≈ 1.9x the market cap, delivery ~24%). 41x trailing earnings — in line with Ratnamani and Venus Pipes, which have higher margins.

**The Shanti Gold link.** Shanti Gold International (whose deep-dive is in this tab) bought 2,65,000 Ratnaveer shares in the open market on 25-Sep-2026 at about ₹333.33 (₹8.83 cr) — a plain market purchase, not a preferential allotment. Shanti Gold called it about 0.37% of Ratnaveer; on the post-rights share count it is **0.32%**. Shanti Gold says it is not a related-party deal.

### 1. What the company is
- Main board since 11-Sep-2023: NSE RATNAVEER, BSE 543978, ISIN INE05CZ01011. Registered office GIDC Savli (Manjusar), Vadodara.
- Sole individual promoter Vijay R. Sanghavi — Chairman, MD **and CFO**. Seema Sanghavi (wife) became executive director in Apr-2026. Frequent company-secretary and independent-director changes since listing.
- Auditor Pankaj R. Shah & Associates (since Feb-2022, after the previous auditor resigned; re-appointed Sep-2026; unmodified opinion; ₹5.5 lakh fee). Rating Infomerics A- (Stable) / A2+ (Apr-2026).
- Plants: Units I–II at Savli (sheets, washers, hooks, pipes), Unit III Waghodia (scrap melting), Unit IV Vatva (rolling; leased). A plot is leased from a promoter-group firm at ₹6 lakh a month. Dormant UAE subsidiary.

**Product mix (latest company slide; year label ambiguous)**

| Product | Share of revenue |
|---|---:|
| Finishing sheets | 52.4% |
| Washers | 14.7% |
| Sheet-metal parts (incl. solar hooks) | 11.0% |
| Scrap | 9.0% |
| Pipes and tubes | 6.5% |
| Nuts and bolts | 5.5% |

**Volume and realisation**

| | FY25 | FY26 |
|---|---:|---:|
| Volume processed (MT) | 36,129 | 46,668 (+29%) |
| Revenue per kg (our calc) | ₹246.9 | ₹229.0 |
| Company EBITDA per tonne (₹) | 25,028 | 26,011 |

- Stated capacity 41,000 MTPA — below the 46,668 MT "processed" in FY26 (definitions differ; utilisation not disclosed).
- Customers: top-1 18%, top-5 45%, top-10 56%; mostly via distributors on purchase orders. Suppliers: top-1 39%, top-10 71%. Raw material ~87–90% of revenue (FY21–23); the MD says cost increases are passed on, but no formula is disclosed.

**Exports: decks vs audited accounts**

| Year | Audited export sales (₹ cr) | Share of revenue |
|---|---:|---:|
| FY23 (RHP) | — | 19.2% |
| FY24 | 44.94 | 7.5% |
| FY25 | 49.91 | 5.6% |
| FY26 | 55.18 | **5.2%** |
| Q1 FY27 | 9.96 | 3.2% |

- FY26 exports by country: Germany ₹29.6 cr, Spain 8.4, Italy 7.1, USA 3.9, France 2.3, UK 1.2. FY26 foreign-exchange earnings reported: only ₹2.68 cr. US tariff exposure is small on audited numbers.

### 2. Growth
| ₹ cr | FY23 | FY24 | FY25 | FY26 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Revenue | 479.75 | 595.38 | 891.88 | **1,068.74** |
| Growth | — | +24.1% | +49.8% | +19.8% |
| Gross margin | 11.8% | 14.0% | 15.4% | 16.5% |
| EBITDA (ex other income) | 47.0 | 49.98 | 86.39 | 112.21 |
| EBITDA margin | 9.8% | 8.4% | 9.7% | 10.5% |
| Profit after tax | 25.04 | 31.05 | 46.82 | **64.31** |

**Quarters (₹ cr)**

| | Q1 FY26 | Q2 FY26 | Q3 FY26 | Q4 FY26 | Q1 FY27 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Revenue | 264.6 | 285.9 | 269.3 | 249.0 | **314.6** |
| EBITDA margin | 10.2% | 9.9% | 10.6% | 11.4% | 10.2% |
| Other income | 0.3 | 2.0 | 0.0 | 7.3 | 3.8 |
| Profit after tax | 15.0 | 15.4 | 16.9 | 17.0 | **18.2** |

- FY26 tax rate 15.4% (current tax only ₹5.2 cr). ROE ≈ 12.4% on average equity.

### 3. Cash, balance sheet and capital raising — the weak spot
| ₹ cr, 31-Mar | FY24 | FY25 | FY26 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Inventory | 244.9 | 292.9 | 289.4 |
| Receivables | 44.8 | 65.6 | **174.6** |
| Advances to suppliers | 24.7 | 52.7 | **169.5** |
| Payables | 43.9 | 120.7 | 222.4 |
| Gross debt | 207.2 | 195.1 | 335.0 |
| Cash + FDs | — | 65.9 | 268.9 |
| Net worth | 252.1 | 370.9 | 669.2 |
| Operating cash flow | 12.35 | 94.93 | **−48.41** |
| Capex | 66.0 | 138.1 | 114.5 |
| Free cash flow | −53.7 | −43.2 | **−162.9** |

- FY25 operating cash flow was flattered by ₹31 cr of capital-goods creditors (reversed in FY26); ex that, FY25 ≈ ₹64 cr and FY26 ≈ −₹22 cr.
- An export-incentive receivable of ₹16.68 cr has not moved in two years.
- Large FDs are pledged while ₹286 cr of short-term borrowing is outstanding; borrowing limit raised from ₹900 cr to ₹1,500 cr at the 26-Sep-2026 AGM.

### 4. Future scope
- **Copper-clad laminates (CCL):** ECMS approval (31-Mar-2026) for FR-4 CCL at Alindra, Savli — 15.84 lakh sheets a year in Phase 1, up to 79.2 lakh over five lines. India is ~100% import-dependent. Cost stated three ways: ₹338 cr (ECMS), ₹472 cr (Gujarat policy), ₹351 cr + ₹250 cr working capital (call). ~60% complete in Jul-2026; start slipped from Sep- to Nov-2026; Chinese machinery; no customer orders confirmed. Wipro, Kaynes and Syrma are entering too.
- **Guidance:** FY27 revenue ₹1,350–1,500 cr; ~₹2,500 cr in ~3 years (₹750 cr CCL + ₹1,800 cr stainless). A European precision-parts acquisition is in due diligence.
- **Industry:** India stainless demand grows ~7–9%; imports surged (Apr-2026 +65% y/y); anti-dumping duty on cold-rolled flats still pending (deadline Mar-2027) — duty-free imports help a processor's input costs. EU CBAM now covers washers and fasteners; EU rooftop solar is shrinking (a headwind for solar hooks).

### Bull case vs bear case
| Bull | Bear |
|---|---|
| ~30% revenue CAGR; margins edging up; Q1 FY27 +19% | ~₹815 cr raised in three years; ₹150 cr of QIP money idle in pledged FDs while raising ₹330 cr more |
| CCL import-substitution plant with ECMS support | CCL cost stated three ways, delayed, no orders, strong competitors |
| Rating upgraded to A-; volume +29% in FY26 | Free cash flow −₹260 cr over three years; receivables and supplier advances ballooning |
| Heavy capital already raised for growth | Export claims contradict audited accounts; promoter at 38.7% with cheap warrants; 41x P/E after +145% in six months |

**What X is saying**

Bulls cite India's import dependence and management's CCL margin targets. The recurring worry, on both X and ValuePickr, is **repeated equity dilution and weak cash conversion**: @shiladitya4u's CCL post itself lists cash burn and frequent dilution as the key risks. - **The Ratnamani link** (@ipo_mantra, Sep-2023): the post calls the 7.48% holders promoters of Ratnamani Metals. The RHP describes them only as extended family of Ratnaveer's promoter, and no filing read this run names them as Ratnamani promoters.
- **Bulk deal of 4,00,000 shares by one buyer (Jul-2024)** (@mystockedge). The NSE bulk-deal record for that date was not retrieved this run.
- **"Avoid on promoter background"** (@RupakRoyC). The post gives no evidence; this is an opinion.
- **ValuePickr (03-Sep-2026) notes from a promoter interview:** CCL pilot production from **Jan-2027**, all five lines by FY28, FY28 revenue ₹2,100 cr, a ₹5,000 cr revenue target for FY31. The interview is not a filing, and the Jan-2027 date conflicts with the company's own filings (below).

### Where X disagrees with the filings
- **QIP discount numbers are swapped.** @_Investor_Feed_ wrote a "7.46% discount (₹4.89)". The closing intimation says a discount of **4.89% (₹7.46 a share)** to the floor price of ₹152.46.

- A ValuePickr post says **promoters bought in the QIP** at ~₹145. The QIP allottees were offshore funds (see the card); the promoter's rise from 42.74% (Mar-2026) to 45.49% (Jun-2026) came from warrant conversion (shareholding filings), not from the QIP.

**What ValuePickr is saying**
There is an active dedicated thread, "Ratnaveer precision a newly headed steel company", started 12-Dec-2023: 42 posts, last post 22-Sep-2026, about 11,100 views. All 42 were read. A further mention in the Shanti Gold thread (28-Sep-2026) asks why Shanti Gold bought Ratnaveer shares; nobody has answered. The tone has turned from early enthusiasm (guidance beaten, "value buy") to scepticism. In 2026 the debate is the copper-clad-laminate (CCL) plan against frequent equity dilution, weak cash conversion and governance. One member links an external post raising promoter concerns, and two others say it puts them off. A technical sub-debate asks whether a maker of bare CCL sheets can find buyers when customers mostly want finished PCBs.

### Threads

| Shanti Gold- Sky Gold in making? (post #7) | mention | 6 | 28-Sep-2026 | [thread](https://forum.valuepickr.com/t/shanti-gold-sky-gold-in-making/224020/7) |

### Points members raise

| Capital subsidies and interest support cut the effective CCL project cost | Bare CCL sheets vs finished PCBs: few domestic buyers and well-funded rivals (yash.s, Aarti) |
| — | Management's numbers differ between interviews (jay_jariwala123) |

### New verified data from the forum
| Data point | Primary source that confirms it |
|---|---|
| **CCL incentives as stated by the MD:** a ~50% capital subsidy (25% from the central government and 25% from the state); an interest subvention under which the company bears about 2% of a ~9% loan rate; 15% exemption on power cost; and exemption on logistics costs for inputs and imported machinery | Q4 FY26 earnings-call transcript (call 14-May-2026, filed 21-May-2026) |

Phase-1 line: ₹108 cr revenue, ₹22 cr EBITDA, ₹12 cr PAT. The deck's 11% CCL PAT margin is lower than the 13% the MD gave on the May call | Q1 FY27 investor presentation, 27-Jul-2026 (NSE) |
| **The guidance track record** that members cite checks out. The FY24 annual report targeted FY25 total income of ₹730 cr and EBITDA of ₹83.67 cr; FY25 came in at ₹891.88 cr revenue and ₹86.39 cr EBITDA. The May-2025 results release targeted ₹1,600 cr in 2–3 years at 13% EBITDA / 8.5% PAT, with a ₹232 cr order book; by May-2026 the target was ~₹2,500 cr | FY24 annual report ("Looking Ahead"); board outcome and results release, 14-May-2025 (NSE); card figures |

That matches the card's Aug–Nov 2024 trade-for-trade (BE) spell and anjeshv4's explanation. Ratnaveer's name on the ESM list itself was not read | NSE circular NSE/SURV/63361, 09-Aug-2024 |

### Claims on the forum not verified
- FY27 revenue of ₹1,500 cr before CCL, FY28 ₹2,100 cr (₹1,750 cr legacy + ₹350 cr CCL), FY31 ₹5,000 cr with ₹525 cr PAT — atishay_jain1, notes from a YouTube interview — not in any filing read; the May-2026 call gave FY27 ₹1,350 cr and ~₹2,500 cr in three years.
- CCL pilot production from Jan-2027 — atishay_jain1 — the Q1 FY27 deck says Line-1 commissioning is "on track for November 2026".
- An interest subsidy of ₹10 cr a year for 7 years (₹70 cr) and a first CCL line costing ₹84 cr — atishay_jain1 — not found; the May call described the subsidy as an interest rate cut, not a rupee amount.

### Where the forum disagrees with the filings
- **"~400 cr QIP" approved in Nov-2024 and postponed (SahilPatani, AnkitAgrawal):** the Nov-2024 plan was not a QIP.
