ideas.name: GP Eco Solutions India Ltd
ideas.trigger: sme: deep-dive on request — NSE Emerge solar-inverter distributor / assembler (Sungrow, own Invergy brand), BESS and solar EPC; FY26 revenue +68% / PAT +310%; ₹124 cr preferential + warrant issue Jul-2026; promoter pledge rose to 55.5% of promoter shares
ideas.thesis:
**In plain words.**
- **What it is:** a Noida company that mainly sells solar inverters — as one of North India's larger distributors for China's Sungrow, and under its own "Invergy" brand (assembled in India, with imported parts) — plus battery storage systems (BESS) and ground-mounted solar projects (EPC) for factories and the PM-KUSUM farm-solar scheme.
- **Growth is fast:** FY26 revenue ₹414 cr (+68%), profit to owners ₹40.1 cr (from ₹10.4 cr). Margins jumped as the mix moved from plain distribution (~76% → 53% of sales) to its own inverters and EPC.
- **But cash did not follow:** receivables tripled to ₹195 cr (172 days). Reported operating cash flow (+₹29 cr) includes ₹35.6 cr of new short-term borrowing — take that out and it was negative. Free cash flow ≈ −₹60 cr. 74% of year-end "cash" was uncleared cheques.
- **Promoters have pledged their shares:** the pledged share of promoter holding went from ~5% (Sep-2025) to 29% (Mar-2026) to **55.5% (Jul-2026)** — a third of the whole company. The FY26 annual report shows why: promoter shares secure the company's own high-cost loans — ₹7.5 cr from Satin Finserv at 16.5% and ₹10 cr from Rajasthan Securities (a broker) at 16% — each with 2.5x share cover. No pledge-creation disclosure was found in NSE's feed.
- **The auditor raised flags:** it was not shown the monthly stock statements filed with the banks; loans to subsidiaries are interest-free and overdue beyond 90 days; it says the company "needs more strong ERP system for recovery from debtors and stock management"; the MD took and repaid ₹6.6 cr of loans from the company during the year. These internal-control remarks repeat in FY24, FY25 and FY26, and the FY25 secretarial audit notes that the promoters' encumbrance (pledge) disclosure under SAST 31(4) was not made. The previous statutory auditor resigned during FY24; NKMR was appointed in Nov-2023, seven months before the IPO.
- **Disclosure quality is weak:** a ₹121.9 cr order was quietly cut to ₹76.9 cr 13 months later, and part of it had already been announced as a "new" order; order values and customers are often left blank; guidance of "3x" revenue became "₹550–600 cr" and the actual was ₹414 cr.
- **Price:** ₹402 is only 12.5x FY26 earnings — in line with SME solar peers — but 35% below its Sep-2025 peak. The ₹124 cr Jul-2026 issue (100% for working capital) brought in two Mauritius funds with ~6% each.

### 1. What the company is
- NSE Emerge (SME) only, listed 24-Jun-2024; symbol GPECO, ISIN INE0S7E01015. Registered office Noida. Indian GAAP. Auditor NKMR & Co (unmodified FY26 opinion; two different firm registration numbers appear in filings).
- Promoters: Deepak Pandey (MD), Anju Pandey, Astik Mani Tripathi; Chairman Pradeep Kumar Pandey (ex-IREDA). CFO changed Aug-2026 (the previous CFO stays as "advisor").
- Group: Invergy India (100%; own-brand inverters and BESS), AN3 Techno Power (51%; BESS assembly, "FuelON", Dasna UP), GPES Green Projects (EPC), GPES Solar 1–10 (PM-KUSUM / IPP power-sale SPVs), and an Invergy Medicare trading arm.
- Chinese supply chain: Sungrow (distributed), TBEA central inverters (resold), imported lithium cells, Sinexcel BESS testers. Invergy's local content is said to reach ">50% by Dec-2026" — i.e., below 50% today.

**Revenue mix (management figures)**

| Segment | FY25 | FY26 | FY27 indicative |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Distribution (Sungrow etc.) | 76% | 53% | ~13% |
| Own manufacturing (Invergy) | 17% | 31% | ~53% |
| EPC | 7% | 16% | ~33% |

- No audited segment split. FY25 annual report: sales ₹241.05 cr = inverters ₹140.21 cr (58%), modules ₹78.26 cr (32%), other ₹22.58 cr; **Sungrow alone was ₹115.80 cr — 82.6% of inverter sales**. FY24: 100% domestic, 99.5% B2B, >80% from UP, Uttarakhand, Punjab, Delhi and Haryana.
- Standalone (mostly distribution) gross margin is only 14.4%; the margin gain sits in the subsidiaries. In-house inverters assembled: 4,338 (FY25) → 16,529 (FY26); PCBs and casings are bought in. Permanent staff 13 (FY24) → 28 → 45 (FY26).

### 2. Growth
| ₹ cr (consolidated) | FY24 | FY25 | FY26 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Revenue | 138.44 | 246.43 | **414.38** |
| Growth | — | +78% | +68% |
| Gross margin | — | 12.4% | 21.2% |
| EBITDA (ex other income) | — | 15.9 | 59.3 |
| EBITDA margin | — | 6.4% | 14.3% |
| Profit before tax | 9.96 | 14.06 | 53.96 |
| Profit after tax (owners) | 7.33 (total) | 10.36 | **40.12** |
| EPS (₹) | 8.68 | 8.85 | 33.91 |

| ₹ cr | H1 FY26 | H2 FY26 |
|---|---:|---:|
| Revenue | 121.47 | **292.91** |
| Gross margin | 22.0% | 20.9% |
| Profit after tax (owners) | 10.40 | 29.72 |

- FY25 profit appears three ways across filings (₹10.46 / 10.36 / 10.24 cr).
- Guidance: Nov-2025 "3x" (₹700–750 cr) for FY26 → Jun-2026 reframed as "₹550–600 cr" → actual ₹414 cr. FY27 guided at 2–3x revenue; management said H1 FY27 would be "one of the lowest".

### 3. Cash, balance sheet and pledges — the weak spot
| ₹ cr | Mar-25 | Mar-26 |
|---|---:|---:|
| Trade receivables | 64.30 | **195.11** |
| Inventory | 18.74 | 56.64 |
| Payables | 49.94 | 140.41 |
| Other current liabilities | 10.89 | 69.41 |
| Borrowings | 33.09 | **108.97** |
| Cash & bank (of which uncleared cheques) | 12.12 | 19.70 (14.60) |
| Fixed assets (PPE + CWIP) | 20.96 | 80.86 |
| Net worth (owners) | 64.88 | 109.15 |

| ₹ cr | FY25 | FY26 |
|---|---:|---:|
| Operating cash flow, reported | 22.33 | 29.33 |
| of which short-term borrowing booked inside it | 19.83 | 35.55 |
| Operating cash flow ex borrowing | ≈ 2.5 | **≈ −6.2** |
| Capex | 18.68 | 53.57 |
| Free cash flow (ex borrowing) | ≈ −16 | **≈ −60** |

- Working capital (FY26 days): receivables 172 (95 in FY25), inventory 63, payables ~157. Management proposes channel financing for its ~40 dealers — the receivables look like dealer credit more than DISCOM dues (inference).
- Net debt ≈ ₹89 cr at Mar-26 (≈ ₹104 cr counting uncleared cheques out of cash). Infomerics assigned IVR BBB (Stable) / A3+ on 25-Sep-2026.
- Receivables ageing (consolidated): ₹11.07 cr of ₹195.11 cr is over 6 months; no bad-debt provision; ₹4.48 cr is owed by SAR Renewables — the MD's wife's proprietorship, which *sold* goods to GP Eco (₹10.9 cr in FY24, ₹3.6 cr in FY25) yet sits on GP Eco's books as a receivable. The ageing doesn't roll forward: Mar-24 shows nothing older than 2 years, Mar-25 shows ₹1.19 cr older than 3 years. No expected-credit-loss provision in any year. Customer advances jumped to ₹59.4 cr (from ₹7.7 cr).

**Lenders (FY26 annual report)**

| Lender | Facility | Rate | Security |
|---|---|---:|---|
| Satin Finserv | business loan ₹7.50 cr | 16.50% | Anju Pandey's shares (2.5x) + ₹75 lakh FD lien |
| Rajasthan Securities | term loan ₹10.00 cr | 16.00% | Anju Pandey's shares (2.5x) |
| SBI | cash credit ₹12.50 cr | EBR + 1.25% | — |
| IndusInd | cash credit ₹6 cr | Repo + 3.40% | Noida properties owned by Pradeep Kumar Pandey |
| HDFC | overdraft ₹3 cr | — | Dasna land owned by Invergy Medicare |
| AU Small Finance Bank | ₹9.16 cr | 9.75% | Jhalawar PM-KUSUM project |

- All facilities carry the three promoters' personal guarantees.

**Promoter pledge (shareholding-pattern filings)**

| Date | Shares pledged | % of promoter holding |
|---|---:|---:|
| Sep-2025 | 3,64,619 | ~5% |
| Mar-2026 | 21,30,553 | 29% |
| Jul-2026 | **40,65,981** | **55.5%** (≈ 33% of the company) |

- Jul-2026 by person: Anju Pandey 22,96,953 of 36,00,000; Deepak Pandey 16,01,428 of 32,33,600; Astik Tripathi 1,67,000 of 3,70,000. No Reg 31 pledge-creation disclosure found; NSE's pledge data returned empty; the promoters' Apr-2026 annual declaration says no encumbrance "other than those already disclosed". The Jul-2026 pledge coincides with the promoters paying ₹6.37 cr upfront on ₹25.5 cr of warrants.

### 4. Future scope
- **Orders:** Jul–Aug 2026 disclosures total ≈ ₹219 cr (0.53x FY26 revenue): KPI Green tracker/MMS supply for SJVN Khavda (₹57.2 cr + ₹58.3 cr), an Invergy inverter/BESS package (₹72.1 cr; buyers "to be disclosed separately" — not found), E-KORS DISCOM inverters (₹18.2 cr), Neelkanth Rolling Mills 4 MW (₹13.0 cr). No confirmed order book is disclosed; management declined to give one on the Jun-2026 call.
- **BESS:** Dasna plant plans moved from "5 GWh by Q3 FY26" to "3 GWh by 30-Sep-2026"; capex guidance from ₹30–40 cr to ~₹200 cr. Module/cell plans (a ₹1,000 cr MP MoU) were "dropped… postponed".
- **IPP:** a 100 MW solar park SPV has 765 kV grid connectivity (project ~₹350 cr — funding not shown); 15 MW PM-KUSUM power sale to MP (PPAs Jun-2026).
- **Industry:** India added a record 44.6 GW of solar in FY26 (16.3 GW distributed, incl. 7.6 GW PM-KUSUM); PM Surya Ghar passed 50 lakh homes (target 75 lakh by Dec-2026) — the market for residential inverters. PM-KUSUM's current timeline ends Sep-2026 (PPA projects to Mar-2027) with a 2.0 version being prepared. DISCOM legacy dues are down to ₹3,330 cr. ALMM List-II (domestic cells) applies to government-backed projects from Jun-2026.

### Bull case vs bear case
| Bull | Bear |
|---|---|
| Revenue +68%, margins up as own-brand inverters and EPC grow | 55.5% of promoter shares pledged, no pledge disclosures found |
| Rooftop (PM Surya Ghar), KUSUM and BESS demand at record levels | Operating cash flow negative once borrowing is taken out; receivables 172 days |
| 12.5x P/E, ~10x EV/EBITDA — cheap vs growth, ROE ~46% | Order cut 37% and re-announced; guidance rewritten; frequent NSE queries |
| New ₹124 cr of equity for working capital; BBB rating | Chinese inverter/cell dependence; heavy dilution (28.5 lakh warrants outstanding) |

ideas.name: Trishakti Industries Ltd
ideas.trigger: filing: CAPEX - Trishakti Industries disclosed on 28-Sep-2026 (15:07 IST, Reg 30 press release) that it has PLACED a purchase order with XCMG worth Rs 105.39 cr for 60 machines - 11 crawler cranes (ten 150-tonne, one 250-tonne), 10 fifty-tonne truck cranes and 39 XGS-series articulated boom lifts - described as part of the balance Rs 130-140 cr of a cumulative Rs 400 cr capex plan. It is a fleet capex, not an order won: Trishakti is the buyer.
ideas.thesis:
**Read the filing before anything else: the direction of this order is the opposite of how it scans.** BSE's own classifier files it under *Award of Order / Receipt of Order*, and the day's scan scored it as an ORDER signal. The press release, opened and read in full (4 pages), says Trishakti **issued** a Rs 105.39 cr purchase order **to** XCMG, the Chinese construction-machinery maker. Nobody has awarded Trishakti anything. This is a fleet purchase - capital going out, capacity coming in - and every number below is framed that way.

**What the business physically does.** Trishakti Industries (BSE 531279, no NSE listing; also on the Calcutta Stock Exchange) rents heavy lifting equipment: crawler cranes, truck-mounted cranes, all-terrain cranes, piling rigs and manlifters, with lifting capability up to 750 MT. The FY26 annual report states a fleet of **143 machines** at 31-Mar-2026, deployed to 100+ customers across 25+ industries, with **Renewable Energy the largest single vertical at about 48% of the deployed fleet**. The customer takes the machine for a project's duration; Trishakti carries the capital cost, the depreciation and the maintenance, and earns rental linked to utilisation. The one physical unit that drives revenue is therefore **a machine-year**, and the one ratio that matters is rental revenue per machine at the utilisation achieved.

**The scale-up already on the record (audited, FY26 annual report).**

| | FY2025 | FY2026 | change |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Revenue from operations (Rs cr) | 14.99 | 27.85 | +85.7% |
| Other income (Rs cr) | 2.03 | 4.60 | +126.9% |
| EBITDA (Rs cr) | 6.28 | 20.21 | +221.9% |
| Depreciation (Rs cr) | 1.18 | 6.82 | +478.7% |
| Finance costs (Rs cr) | 1.47 | 3.88 | +163.7% |
| PAT (Rs cr) | 3.55 | 7.66 | +115.9% |
| Fleet (machines) | ~29 (fleet "nearly quintupled" in FY26) | 143 | - |
| Capex deployed (Rs cr) | 48.80 | 210.00 | - |
| Total assets (Rs cr) | 67.96 | 289.10 | +325% |

Q1 FY27, filed with BSE: revenue **Rs 14.38 cr against Rs 4.08 cr** a year earlier (**+252%**), PAT **Rs 4.30 cr against Rs 0.91 cr** (+372%). One quarter of FY27 has already produced more revenue than the whole of FY25. The company states **near-100% fleet utilisation** through FY26 and Q1 FY27, and today's release puts the fleet at **approximately 155-158 machines** as of the Q1 FY27 earnings call of 23-Jul-2026, with an **executable order book of about Rs 70-72 cr for FY27**.

**Why the growth is credible and where the doubt sits.** The revenue is not a claim; it is filed quarterly and it accelerated for four consecutive quarters (Rs 4.08 cr, 6.65, 8.00, 9.11, then 14.38). Utilisation near 100% while the fleet quintupled is the non-trivial part - fleet growth without utilisation is the classic warning sign, and it did not happen here. What is unproven is whether the *returns* justify the capital: statutory **ROCE was 11.83% in FY26** against management's stated aspiration of 22-25% on incremental capex, and the funding structure (below) is where this idea is most likely to break.

**One arithmetic inconsistency in the company's own release, recorded not resolved.** It says the 60 new machines take the fleet to "230 units", and separately restates a target of "200+ units by FY27". 155-158 plus 60 is 215-218. The three numbers do not reconcile; the release does not give a delivery schedule, so how many of the 60 machines earn rental in FY27 at all is unknown.
ideas.model:
**Revenue per machine, measured rather than assumed.** Two anchors exist and they differ, so both are shown.

| basis | revenue | fleet | revenue per machine-year |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| FY26 full year | Rs 27.85 cr | average of ~29 opening and 143 closing = ~86 | **Rs 32.4 lakh** |
| Q1 FY27 annualised (x4) | Rs 14.38 cr x 4 = Rs 57.52 cr | ~156.5 (company's own 155-158) | **Rs 36.8 lakh** |

The Q1 FY27 figure is the better forward anchor: it is the most recent filed quarter and the fleet was not doubling inside it. It is still one quarter annualised, and crane rental is not perfectly even across quarters - that is a stated limitation, not a hidden one.

**What the 60 machines can add, at the company's own numbers.**

- Fleet after delivery: 155-158 + 60 = **215-218 machines** (using the release's arithmetic inputs, not its "230").
- At Rs 36.8 lakh per machine-year: 218 x 0.368 = **Rs 80.2 cr of revenue** at full deployment, against Rs 27.85 cr in FY26 and a Rs 57.5 cr Q1 FY27 run-rate.
- **The margin that matters is not the headline one.** The annual report's "EBITDA margin 62.3%" is EBITDA divided by *total income* (Rs 20.21 cr / Rs 32.44 cr). Measured against revenue from operations, and excluding other income, operating EBITDA was Rs 15.62 cr on Rs 27.85 cr = **56.1%**. Using 56.1%: Rs 80.2 cr of revenue gives about **Rs 45.0 cr of operating EBITDA**.

**Then the two costs that scale with the asset base, which is where the case thins.**

- **Depreciation.** FY26 depreciation of Rs 6.82 cr on average property, plant and equipment of Rs 112.7 cr (Rs 36.11 cr opening, Rs 189.38 cr closing) is an effective **6.05% a year** - about a 16-year life. Add Rs 105.39 cr of new machines plus the Rs 25.82 cr already in capital work-in-progress and PPE reaches roughly **Rs 320 cr**, implying depreciation of about **Rs 19.4 cr** a year once the fleet is in service, against Rs 6.82 cr in FY26.
- **Finance cost.** FY26 finance cost of Rs 3.88 cr on average total borrowings of Rs 59.05 cr is an effective 6.6%, and that rate does not capture the Rs 156.01 cr of *other current financial liabilities* the company attributes to "equipment financing arrangements". If the Rs 105.39 cr is funded on similar terms at roughly 9%, finance cost rises by about Rs 9.5 cr to **Rs 13.4 cr**. The 9% is an assumption and is flagged as such - the release states no funding plan.

**The bridge, with the assumptions visible.**

| line | Rs cr | source |
|---|---:|---|
| Revenue at 218 machines | 80.2 | Q1 FY27 revenue per machine x fleet |
| Operating EBITDA at 56.1% | 45.0 | FY26 operating margin ex other income |
| less depreciation | (19.4) | FY26 effective 6.05% on ~Rs 320 cr PPE |
| less finance cost | (13.4) | FY26 base plus ~9% on Rs 105 cr (assumed) |
| = PBT excluding other income | **12.2** | |
| PAT at a 25% tax rate | **9.2** | FY26 effective rate was 19.5%; 25% used as the normalised rate |

On 1.656 cr shares (equity capital Rs 331.15 lakh at Rs 2 face), that is **EPS of about Rs 5.55**; fully diluted for the 16.18 lakh outstanding warrants, about **Rs 5.06**. Add back other income at the FY26 level of Rs 4.60 cr and PAT reaches about Rs 12.6 cr, **EPS Rs 6.93 diluted**.

**The conclusion the arithmetic forces.** Nearly doubling the fleet roughly doubles revenue, but depreciation triples and finance cost more than triples, so **EPS does not double**. At the 2026-09-28 close of Rs 243.05 the forward PE on the Rs 6.93 case is about **35x** - essentially unchanged from the trailing multiple. This capex buys scale; on these inputs it does not by itself buy a re-rating. What would change that is revenue per machine rising rather than holding, or the funding coming as equity rather than as more current liabilities.
ideas.valuation:
**Trishakti at the 2026-09-28 close of Rs 243.05.**

| measure | value | basis |
|---|---:|---|
| Market cap | Rs 392.1 cr | BSE scrip master, this run |
| FY26 EPS | Rs 4.67 | BSE detailed results, FY26 audited |
| PE on FY26 EPS | **52.0x** | 243.05 / 4.67 |
| Trailing-4-quarter EPS | Rs 6.74 | Q2-Q4 FY26 (0.98 + 1.50 + 1.65) + Q1 FY27 (2.61) |
| PE on trailing 4 quarters | **36.1x** | 243.05 / 6.74 |
| Net worth 31-Mar-2026 | Rs 44.75 cr | audited: share capital 3.31 + other equity 41.44 |
| Price to book | **about 8.8x** | 392.1 / 44.75, before any warrant conversion |
| FY26 ROCE | 11.83% | company's own ratio table |
| FY26 ROE | 21.62% | company's own ratio table |

*BSE's company header reports EPS 6.54, PE 37.16, PB 32.98 and ROE 88.72 for this scrip. The EPS and PE are close to the trailing-four-quarter figures computed above, but PB 32.98 and ROE 88.72 cannot be reconciled with audited net worth of Rs 44.75 cr and the company's own stated ROE of 21.62%. The audited figures are used above and BSE's header ratios are treated as unreliable for this scrip.*

**The one real listed comparator.** The dossier's automatic peer set is useless here - BSE files Trishakti under *Diversified Commercial Services*, which returns staffing, finance and alcohol companies. The genuine comparator is **Sanghvi Movers (BSE 530073)**, India's established listed crane-rental company, read from its BSE header this run:

| | Trishakti | Sanghvi Movers |
|---|---:|---:|
| Market cap (Rs cr) | 392 | 3,953 |
| PE | 36.1x trailing | **24.35x** (19.31x consolidated) |
| Price to book | ~8.8x | **3.64x** |
| Operating margin | 62.30% (on total income) | 49.18% |
| ROE | 21.62% | 14.96% |
| Net profit margin | 27.51% | 20.29% |

**So the re-rating case, stated honestly, is weak on multiples.** Trishakti already trades at a ~48% PE premium and a ~2.4x price-to-book premium to the incumbent peer, while earning its higher margins on a balance sheet levered 1.90x with a current ratio of 0.37x. The bull case cannot be "it is cheap"; it has to be "the fleet compounds at near-100% utilisation and revenue per machine holds", and the price already carries a good deal of that. The market cap of Rs 392 cr does sit inside the Rs 300-7,500 cr band where the three-year study found 5x runs concentrate, and the stock has not had a volume explosion - volume on 2026-09-28 was **0.4x** the 60-day median, which the same study says is neither good nor bad evidence (81% of 5x runs had a volume spike and so did 78% of the stocks that went nowhere).
ideas.red_flags:
- **The balance sheet is the main risk, and it is not in the borrowings line.** Total assets of Rs 289.10 cr at 31-Mar-2026 are funded by net worth of just Rs 44.75 cr, total borrowings of Rs 85.18 cr, and **Rs 156.01 cr of "other financial liabilities" inside current liabilities - up from Rs 8.54 cr, a rise of 1,727%**. This single line is larger than all borrowings combined and larger than three times net worth. The company attributes it to "increased current liabilities linked to equipment financing arrangements". Note 22 was not read in full this run, so what exactly it contains, when it falls due and on what terms is **unknown** - and it is the most important unknown about this company.
- **Current ratio fell from 1.09x to 0.37x** (-66%), the company's own disclosure. Current liabilities are roughly 2.7x current assets.
- **Cash and equivalents are Rs 0.58 cr**, down 48.4% from Rs 1.12 cr, against Rs 105.39 cr of equipment now on order.
- **Debt-equity rose from 1.26x to 1.90x**, debt service coverage fell from 1.58x to 1.43x, interest coverage 3.45x. The company describes the leverage as "a conscious trade-off" and says the current ratio is one it is "actively managing".
- **The board is seeking to raise the borrowing limit from Rs 400 cr to Rs 1,000 cr** (AGM resolution, item 4 in the notice). That is 2.5x the current cap and 22x FY26 net worth - an intention to lever much further.
- **Receivables.** Trade receivables rose 94.3% to Rs 20.19 cr. The company's own trade-receivables turnover of 1.82x implies about **201 days** of sales outstanding, and the company names receivables management "an explicit priority for FY27".
- **ROCE of 11.83% is below any plausible blended cost of this capital structure**, and roughly half management's own 22-25% aspiration. Statutory ROCE is the measured number; the aspiration is not.
- **Dilution at a price well below today's.** 16,18,000 warrants were issued at Rs 158.10 to promoters, promoter group and public (board 16-Jul-2025, EGM 13-Aug-2025), with only the minimum 25% (Rs 6.40 cr) received and 18 months to convert; equity shares were also allotted preferentially at Rs 158.10. Two warrant holders had converted by the date of the report. The close today is Rs 243.05.
- **Promoter holding has fallen**, from 68.97% (June 2026) to **67.26%** (02-Sep-2026 disclosure), having been 68.49% in December 2025. Whether the fall is dilution from warrant conversion by non-promoters or promoter selling was not established this run.
- **The headline EBITDA margin is flattered by other income.** Rs 4.60 cr of other income is 14.2% of total income; the stated 62.3% margin is on total income, and operating EBITDA on revenue from operations is 56.1%.
- **Two internal inconsistencies in the company's own FY26 annual report.** Its performance dashboard shows capex deployed of Rs 4,880 lakh in the FY26 column and Rs 21,000 lakh in the FY25 column, while the narrative on the facing page says FY26 deployed Rs 21,000 lakh and FY25 Rs 4,880 lakh - the row is transposed. And the release's fleet arithmetic (above) does not reconcile.
- **Related-party and remuneration detail could not be checked.** The annual report states there were no materially significant related-party transactions, but the Section 197(12) managerial-remuneration statement was **excluded from the dispatched report** and is available only on inspection at the registered office. So promoter salary against profit is unknown, not clean.
- **A material subsidiary that is a finance company.** Trishakti Capital Limited was a material subsidiary in FY26 under Regulation 16(1)(c) and ceases to be one in FY27. Its accounts were not read.
- **The price has already moved:** +61.8% over the 65-day scan window, +91.5% over six months, +65.5% over a year, and it sits 10.8% below the window high of Rs 272.5.
- **What is clean:** the statutory auditors expressed an **unmodified opinion** with no qualification, reservation, adverse remark or disclaimer, and the secretarial audit report likewise.
- **The order study does not transfer to this filing.** The 1,245-filing study measured orders *received*, sized against a trailing year of sales, and found rarity predictive. This is a purchase order *issued*, so neither finding applies. For scale only: Rs 105.39 cr is **3.8x** FY26 revenue of Rs 27.85 cr and **26.9%** of market cap. The count of Trishakti's own prior order or capex announcements could not be established - BSE's per-scrip announcement endpoint returns "No Record Found!" for scrip 531279 (measured three times this run), and the company has no NSE symbol, so the NSE archive covers it either.
ideas.verify:
1. **Note 22, "other financial liabilities" - Rs 156.01 cr.** The single most valuable missing fact. It is the largest item on the balance sheet, it grew 18-fold in one year, and it sits in *current* liabilities against Rs 0.58 cr of cash. Whether it is supplier credit from equipment vendors, finance-lease obligations, or something with a near-term maturity decides whether the fleet is funded or merely deferred. It needs the full FY26 financial statements notes, which this run did not read.
2. **How the Rs 105.39 cr is being paid, and when the 60 machines arrive.** The release states neither a funding source nor a delivery schedule. A quarter-by-quarter delivery profile is what turns the model above from a full-deployment number into an FY27 number. The Q2 FY27 earnings call and any subsequent Reg 30 disclosure on financing would settle it.
3. **Whether rental yield per machine is holding as the fleet doubles.** The whole case rests on Rs 36.8 lakh per machine-year. The Q2 FY27 result against the disclosed fleet count is the direct test, and it arrives within weeks.
4. **Utilisation, independently.** "Near 100%" is management's figure and is not separately verifiable from the filings. Customer or dealer checks, or the mix of machines on hire disclosed in an investor presentation, would corroborate it.
5. **Whether the receivable is collectible.** About 201 days of sales outstanding with Tier-1 names (L&T, Adani and Reliance are the relationships the annual report claims) should not take 200 days. An ageing schedule from the notes, and confirmation of those customer relationships, are both ground work.
6. **The Rs 400 cr to Rs 1,000 cr borrowing limit.** Whether shareholders approved it, and what the board intends to draw, would materially change the leverage picture.
ideas.unknowns:
- **The composition, terms and maturity of the Rs 156.01 cr of other current financial liabilities.** Note 22 was not read.
- **Delivery schedule for the 60 XCMG machines, and therefore how much of the Rs 80 cr revenue case lands in FY27 rather than FY28.**
- **Funding source for the Rs 105.39 cr.** Not stated in the release.
- **The fleet count that reconciles.** 155-158 plus 60 is 215-218; the release says 230 and separately targets 200+. Which is right is unknown.
- **Prior order and capex announcement count**, hence the rarity test: BSE's per-scrip announcement endpoint returns "No Record Found!" for scrip 531279 and there is no NSE listing.
- **Managerial remuneration against profit.** The Section 197(12) statement was excluded from the dispatched annual report.
- **Why promoter holding fell from 68.97% to 67.26%** between June and September 2026 - dilution or sale.
- **Trishakti Capital Limited's accounts**, and what a finance subsidiary does inside an equipment-rental group.
- **Whether the Rs 4.60 cr of other income recurs.** It is 14.2% of total income and 60% of PAT.
- **No investor presentation or concall transcript was read.** BSE's per-scrip announcement feed does not serve this scrip, so only the FY26 annual report, the day's press release and the BSE results series were available. The Q1 FY27 fleet and order-book figures quoted here are the company's own, as restated in today's release, not read from the transcript itself.
- **Q1 FY27 EBITDA**, and therefore whether the 56.1% operating margin held into FY27. The quarterly filing in the BSE series gives revenue, other income and PAT but not the expense split.
ideas.confidence: low: the trigger is verified from the filing itself and it is large - Rs 105.39 cr is 3.8x a trailing year's revenue and 26.9% of market cap - on a company whose revenue rose 85.7% in FY26 and 252% in Q1 FY27 at near-100% utilisation, inside the Rs 300-7,500 cr band where the three-year study found 5x runs concentrate, and with an unmodified audit opinion. Three things hold the confidence down. First, the model's own arithmetic: doubling the fleet roughly doubles revenue but triples depreciation and finance cost, so the forward PE stays near 35x and the multiple does not compress on its own. Second, the funding: Rs 156.01 cr of other current financial liabilities against Rs 0.58 cr of cash, a current ratio of 0.37x and a request to lift the borrowing limit to Rs 1,000 cr - and note 22, which would explain it, was not read. Third, the stock has already risen 91.5% in six months and trades at a 48% PE premium and 2.4x the price-to-book of Sanghvi Movers, the established peer. This is filed as research on a verified trigger with the balance-sheet question open, not as a conclusion.

ideas.thesis:
**In plain words.**
- **What it is:** a Ludhiana company that sells make-up under its own "Recode" brand (350+ SKUs: foundation, primer, setting spray, kajal, lipsticks, brushes). It makes nothing itself — products come from contract manufacturers in India and from Germany/Thailand; it brands, markets and distributes them. It became known after Shark Tank India season 2 (Jan-2023).
- **Where it is listed:** **BSE SME only** (scrip 544755, symbol RECODE, ISIN INE2B6701015). It is *not* on NSE Emerge — the shareholding filing says "NSE Symbol: NOTLISTED" and RECODE is absent from NSE's 25- and 28-Sep bhavcopies.
- **Growth is real on paper:** revenue ₹22.4 cr (FY23) → ₹79.95 cr (FY26); profit ₹0.69 cr → ₹11.22 cr. Gross margin rose from 48% to 62% and EBITDA margin from 6% to 21%.
- **But the best quarter was the one the IPO was priced on.** Subtracting the audited H1 from the prospectus's 9-month accounts gives Oct–Dec 2025 at a 36% EBITDA margin; Jan–Mar 2026 (after the prospectus cut-off) fell to 14%, and receivables jumped ₹5.4 cr in that one quarter.
- **Reporting is sloppy:** the half-year results were re-filed four days later (H2 PAT ₹557 → ₹734 lakh, H1 ₹512 → ₹388 lakh); the press release still carries the wrong numbers; the signed auditor's CARO report contains the drafting note "The highlighted conclusions in this draft must be agreed … before the report is signed"; director pay differs between two sections of the same annual report.
- **Governance churn right after listing:** all three independent directors resigned (13-Jul, 5-Aug, 17-Aug-2026), co-founder/promoter Rahul Sachdeva quit as COO (24-Aug) and was replaced by the MD's son, the CS left (31-Aug). The previous statutory auditor also resigned during FY26.
- **Price:** ₹448.55 = ₹477 cr market cap = **42.5x FY26 EPS on post-IPO shares**, ~6x EV/sales — the stock is up 184% from the ₹158 issue price and 157% from its June low, with seven sessions closing up ~5% in a day. Management guides ≥50% growth in FY27; even hitting that at FY26 margins gives ~28x.

### 1. The business

- 156 employees (Mar-2026), 22–23 stores (3 COCO, 19 FOFO), 6 warehouses, 7 mall kiosks (Aug-2026), first NewU (Dabur's H&B chain) store Aug-2026, Nykaa Now quick-commerce Sep-2026. Management said on 3-Jun-2026 that the FOFO franchise model is "closed for the time being" in favour of dark stores.
- 9M FY26 top customer = 15.94% of net sales, top-10 = 39.4% (names withheld; management calls Nykaa a B2B customer that "buys upfront" under a sale-or-return model). Top-10 suppliers = 87.4% of purchases, top-1 = 21.6%.

ideas.model:
**Revenue model.** There is no single physical unit here: this is a brand that outsources production. Revenue = channels (own website ~33% of sales, marketplaces ~12%, FOFO/B2B/Nykaa ~55%) × stores/reach × product mix. The company does not disclose volumes, store-level sales or SKU counts. The only disclosed drivers are store/kiosk counts, "engaged sessions" (53.5 lakh in 9M FY26 vs 59.7 lakh in FY25) and return on ad spend (5.23x 9M FY26 vs 5.27x FY25 and 7.74x FY23 — falling).

**Guidance arithmetic (management: "at least 50% growth in FY27", EBITDA margin "more or less where it currently is"):**

| ₹ cr | FY26 actual | FY27 at guidance | Arithmetic |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| Revenue | 79.95 | 119.9 | 79.95 × 1.5 |
| EBITDA | 16.54 | 24.8 | 119.9 × 20.7% |
| PAT | 11.22 | 16.8 | 119.9 × 14.0% (FY26 PAT margin) |
| EPS (1,06,44,344 sh) | 10.55 | 15.8 | 16.8 cr ÷ 1.064 cr sh |
| P/E at ₹448.55 | 42.5x | 28.4x | |

Aflairza is excluded (a 33% associate; FY26 sales of ₹8.22 cr; profit not disclosed). ESOP dilution (up to 2.8%) is also excluded.

**Cross-checks and seasonality.**
- H1 (Apr–Sep) is seasonally weak for colour cosmetics (heat and humidity); management says Oct–Dec is the strongest quarter. H1 FY26 revenue was ₹36.94 cr, so +50% means H1 FY27 ≈ ₹55.4 cr (results due by 14-Nov-2026).
- FY26's 20.7% EBITDA margin blends a 16% H1, a 36% Q3 and a 14% Q4. The margin that persisted *after* the IPO pricing period is the 14% Q4 figure. At 14% EBITDA and ~9% PAT on ₹120 cr, EPS would be ~₹10 and P/E ~44x.
- Marketing (advertisement ₹644 lakh + social media ₹539 lakh) was 14.8% of FY26 revenue (18.7% with commissions). Management says it spends "20% of revenue" and will reinvest any margin gains into advertising.
- No credit-rating report was found, so there is no third-party cross-check of revenue expectations.

BSE's own header shows EPS 5.33 and P/E 84.2. ₹5.33 equals the H2 FY26 PAT *as first filed* (₹567.39 lakh, later corrected to ₹734.32 lakh) divided by post-IPO shares. BSE's figure therefore appears to rest on one erroneous half-year; do not use it.

**At the IPO**, the ₹158 price was 38.9x FY25 restated EPS (₹4.06, Recode's own RHP peer table) and ~10.7x annualised 9M FY26 EPS (₹11.13 × 365/275 = ₹14.77, both on pre-IPO shares). The stock now trades at 3x that issue price. At 42.5x FY26 earnings, the market is already paying for the guided 50% growth *and* for FY26's peak margins holding. The re-rating case, in one sentence: if H1 FY27 shows ≥50% growth with ≥20% EBITDA margin and receivable days back under 60, the multiple can hold on a ₹15–16 EPS; if not, the multiple rests on a quarter (Oct–Dec 2025) that has not repeated.

ideas.trigger: sme: deep-dive on request — BSE SME ethnic-wear retailer listed 1-Jul-2026 at ₹106 (opened −20%), ₹83.19 on 28-Sep after two ~20% up-days with no filing; FY26 revenue ₹33.37 cr (+35%), PAT ₹5.19 cr (+9%), but inventory ₹41 cr (123% of sales) not kept in the accounting system, OCF −₹3.19 cr, debt ₹41 cr after a ₹25.5 cr Mumbai auction property, and IPO objects varied within 2 months of listing
ideas.thesis:
**In plain words.**
- **What it is:** an Ahmedabad family business that designs and sells wedding and festive ethnic wear (sherwanis, lehengas, Indo-western, kurta sets) through its own stores. Legal name **Riyaasat Lifestyle Ltd** (CIN now L18100GJ2021PLC126637, incorporated 23-Oct-2021). Promoters: Gaurang R. Galiya (MD), his father Ramanbhai (WTD) and mother Sobhanaben (director).
- **Where it is listed:** **BSE SME only** — scrip **544804**, symbol RIYAASAT, ISIN INE0KYI01012, group M. Not on NSE: the pre-listing shareholding filing says "NSE Symbol: NOTLISTED" and RIYAASAT is absent from NSE's 28-Sep bhavcopy. (The 5-Sep board outcome letter wrongly heads itself "NSE SYMBOL: RIYAASAT".)
- **IPO:** 28,48,800 fresh shares at ₹106 = ₹30.20 cr, listed 1-Jul-2026. It opened at ₹84.80 (−20%), fell to ₹53.02 (13-Aug), and closed ₹83.19 on 28-Sep (−21.5% vs issue) after two back-to-back ~20% up days (25 and 28-Sep) with no price-sensitive filing.
- **Growth on paper is modest, profit is lumpy:** revenue ₹20.93 cr (FY23) → ₹33.37 cr (FY26); PAT ₹1.32 cr → ₹5.19 cr. FY26 revenue +34.6% but PAT only +8.6%. The business is extremely seasonal: H1 FY26 was a **loss of ₹4.89 cr** and H2 a profit of ₹10.08 cr (same pattern in FY25: H1 loss ₹6.27 cr, H2 profit ₹11.05 cr).
- **The core problem is inventory.** Stock rose from ₹5.27 cr (Mar-23) to **₹41.05 cr (Mar-26) = 123% of a year's revenue**. The FY26 P&L took a ₹19.18 cr credit for inventory build-up; purchases were ₹22.47 cr against revenue of ₹33.37 cr, yet reported gross margin is 85%. The audited notes say **"Inventory is not maintained in the accounting system (Tally Prime)"**; the auditor said it could not comment on physical verification; and stock statements given to banks did not agree with the books.
- **Cash does not follow profit:** operating cash flow was negative in 3 of 4 years; cumulative FY23–FY26 OCF −₹5.55 cr against cumulative PAT +₹15.38 cr.
- **Debt jumped to buy real estate:** a Santacruz (W), Mumbai building bought at a Standard Chartered bank auction for ₹25.51 cr (bid 21-Mar-2025) took gross block up by ₹29.51 cr; borrowings went from ₹8.87 cr to **₹41.36 cr** (D/E 2.26x) in FY26. Within two months of listing the company sought to vary IPO objects: ₹13.53 cr of the ₹30.20 cr (working capital ₹9.50 cr + GCP ₹4.03 cr) was already spent by 1-Sep, none of the ₹12.47 cr store capex, and the Mumbai store money is to go into the same Santacruz building where it has won another SARFAESI e-auction (Religare Finvest) for the basement, 3rd and 4th floors — price not disclosed.
- **Price:** ₹83.19 = ₹89.38 cr market cap = **17.2x FY26 EPS on post-IPO shares**, EV/EBITDA ~12.8x on the March-2026 balance sheet. Not expensive on the headline numbers — but the headline numbers rest on an inventory figure that the audit trail does not support well.

### 1. The business
- Product mix (RHP, top-5 products, ₹ lakh, 10M to 31-Jan-2026): lehenga choli 587.71 (21.1%), sherwani 454.68 (16.3%), Indo-western 319.55 (11.5%), kurta set 315.23 (11.3%), suit/tuxedo 172.75 (6.2%). Manufacturing revenue 25.6% / trading revenue 74.4% of 10M FY26.
- Stores (RHP): 6 EBOs — 4 Ahmedabad (Time Square C.G. Road, Ten-11, Iscon Arcade, Stellar Sindhubhavan 9,419 sq ft), 1 Vadodara, 1 Mumbai. Top-2 stores = 54.8% of 10M FY26 revenue (Time Square ₹825 lakh, Santacruz ₹701 lakh). Online only 2.9%.
- 177 employees at 31-Jan-2026 (RHP) / 190 permanent (FY26 annual report); only 12 enrolled in EPF (₹40,000 deposited for Jan-2026) and 32 in ESIC.
- The RHP's own chapters disagree on the Mumbai store: the business overview lists a Santacruz showroom as **owned**, the property table lists the Santacruz "Rhiday" building as **Workshop 3 (owned)** and a leased Goregaon showroom as store 6, and risk factor 19 says **all** stores are leasehold.

### 2. Growth (₹ lakh; FY23–FY25 and 10M FY26 restated per RHP; FY26 audited annual report)
| | FY23 | FY24 | FY25 | 10M FY26 | FY26 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|

ideas.name: Valiant Communications Ltd
ideas.trigger: filing: ORDER - Valiant Communications filed a Reg 30 disclosure on 29-Sep-2026 12:41 IST: a Letter of Award of INR 4,025 lacs (Rs 40.25 cr, inclusive of taxes) from a domestic 'System Integrator (Private)' for supply of communication and grid-protection solutions, end-user the Indian Power Utility Sector, to be executed by 31-12-2028. The stock closed +15.0% at Rs 1,652.10, a 65-day high, on 7.2x its 60-day median volume.
ideas.thesis:
**The filing, read.** The two-page disclosure (BSE, 29-Sep-2026 12:41 IST) states every field in the company's own words: awarding entity **System Integrator (Private)**; scope **"Supply of communication and Grid-protection solution as per the technical requirements"**; domestic; nature **"Supply, services and AMC"**; execution **by 31-12-2028**; size **INR 4,025 Lacs (inclusive of taxes)**; no promoter interest, not a related-party transaction; **"End-user: Indian Power Utility Sector"**. The filing notes the figure is reported gross, i.e. inclusive of indirect taxes, per the SEBI circular of 25-Feb-2025.

**What the business physically does.** Valiant Communications (founded 1993, New Delhi) manufactures communication, transmission, protection, synchronisation, cybersecurity and NAS/SAN storage equipment for power utilities and other critical infrastructure. From the FY2026 annual report and the Q1-FY27 business update, both filed with BSE:

- Product lines: teleprotection (distance protection), IEEE C37.94 line-differential protection communication, phasor measurement units (PMU), grid islanding and WAMS, GPS/GNSS/**NavIC** primary reference clocks and PTP 1588v2 timing, IP/MPLS routers and SDH/PDH multiplexers, network-isolation "kill switch" and PRP switches, ransomware-resilient NAS/SAN storage.
- **"Valiant's Communication and protection equipment has been successfully installed in over 6,000+ power substations globally"** (FY2026 annual report); installations in **110+ countries**, offices in India, USA and UK, 25+ distributors.
- Qualified as a **'Class 1 Local Supplier'** under the Public Procurement (Preference to Make in India) Order, 2017, and registered as a **'Trusted Source'** by the National Security Council Secretariat.
- Revenue split FY2026: **domestic 85.78%, exports 14.22%** (annual report, Corporate Highlights).

The physical unit that drives revenue is a substation bay or a communication/protection node, but the company does not disclose units shipped. The disclosed driver is therefore the **order book**, which it publishes every quarter.

**The order book is the reason this filing is large.** The Q1-FY27 business update (BSE, 12-Aug-2026) prints the series directly:

| Quarter | Gross order book (confirmed), Rs lacs |
|---|---:|
| Q1 FY25 | 2,248 |
| Q2 FY25 | 1,834 |
| Q3 FY25 | 1,271 |
| Q4 FY25 | 10,195 |
| Q1 FY26 | 8,694 |
| Q2 FY26 | 7,667 |
| Q3 FY26 | 7,643 |
| Q4 FY26 | 6,892 |
| **Q1 FY27** | **6,420** |

Read that honestly: the confirmed book has **fallen every quarter since Q4 FY25**, from Rs 101.95 cr to **Rs 64.20 cr at 30-Jun-2026**, because the company has been executing faster than it has been replenishing. Today's Rs 40.25 cr award is **62.7% of that entire confirmed book**. It is the largest single order in the company's 760-day filing history that we could read.

**Order inflow since the book was last published**, each number taken from its own Reg 30 filing, all inclusive of taxes:

| Filed | Awarding entity / end-user | Scope | Execute by | Rs cr |
|---|---|---|---|---:|
| 05-Aug-2026 | Large System Integrator; end-user **Power Grid Corporation of India** | Data storage servers with backup + GPS/NavIC time synchronisation (PGCIL VoIP) | 31-03-2027 | 10.71 |
| 08-Sep-2026 | Indian Power Utilities | Supply and commissioning of communication equipment | not stated in the excerpt read | 9.85 |
| 10-Sep-2026 | System Integrator (Private) | Supply of communication equipment | 30-09-2027 | 13.88 |
| **29-Sep-2026** | **System Integrator (Private); end-user Indian Power Utility Sector** | **Communication + grid protection, supply/services/AMC** | **31-12-2028** | **40.25** |
| | | | **Total** | **74.69** |

Rs 74.69 cr of announced inflow in 55 days, against **Rs 84.11 cr of FY2026 revenue**. Adding it to the Rs 64.20 cr book at 30-Jun-2026 and ignoring Q2 execution (Q2 results are not yet filed) gives roughly **Rs 138.9 cr of gross confirmed work** — the first time in this record that the book exceeds a year of sales.

**Why the end-user matters.** The 05-Aug-2026 filing names **Power Grid Corporation of India** as end-user and the company's own update calls it *"VCL's strategic order into the Data Center application"*, built on equipment already commissioned at THDC Limited. The FY2026 annual report names **Smart Grid and RDSS** (the Revamped Distribution Sector Scheme) as the lead domestic opportunity driver. RDSS smart metering is the single best-performing basket in this repo's government study — 8 names, 12.0x basket median against 3.2x for the market from 30-Jun-2021, 100% made 5x. Valiant is not a smart-meter maker; it sells the communication and protection layer that the same substation-digitisation spend buys. That is an adjacency, not membership, and the note treats it as such.

**Revenue arithmetic, from measured quarters.** All figures standalone, from the BSE detailed-results feed and the Q1-FY27 filing.

| Quarter | Revenue Rs cr | EBITDA Rs cr | PAT Rs cr |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Q1 FY25 | 13.60 | 4.61 | 2.92 |
| Q2 FY25 | 12.68 | 4.44 | 2.78 |
| Q3 FY25 | 8.09 | 0.70 | -0.01 |
| Q4 FY25 | 16.02 | 5.89 | 3.82 |
| Q1 FY26 | 18.12 | 6.68 | 4.46 |
| Q2 FY26 | 20.06 | 7.42 | 4.99 |
| Q3 FY26 | 21.94 | 8.23 | 5.54 |
| Q4 FY26 | 23.99 | 10.02 | 6.67 |
| **Q1 FY27** | **25.14** | **11.63** | **8.08** |

Q1 FY27 against Q1 FY26: revenue **+38.7%**, PAT **+81.2%**. The EBITDA margin the company prints for Q1 FY27 is **46.26%**, against 36.85% a year earlier. Nine consecutive quarters of sequential revenue growth since the Q3 FY25 trough.

**Forward revenue, three ways.** Q1 FY27 actual plus three quarters at a stated sequential rate:

| Sequential growth | FY27 revenue Rs cr | PAT at 28% | PAT at 32% | EPS at 32% | PE at Rs 1,652.10 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 0% (Q1 run-rate held) | 100.6 | 28.2 | 32.2 | 27.5 | 60.0 |
| +5% a quarter | 108.4 | 30.3 | 34.7 | 29.7 | 55.7 |
| +10% a quarter | 116.7 | 32.7 | 37.3 | 31.9 | 51.7 |

The 28-32% PAT-margin band is taken from the last four measured quarters (FY26 full year 25.8%; Q4 FY26 27.8%; Q1 FY27 32.1%) and is an assumption, not guidance — **the company gives no revenue or margin guidance in any document read this run.** Share count 1.169 cr (paid-up capital Rs 1,169 lacs at Rs 10 face value, Q1 FY27 filing); 3,50,000 warrants remain outstanding, so the fully converted count is 1.204 cr.

**Cross-check against the order book.** Rs 138.9 cr gross confirmed work, less roughly 18% indirect tax, is about Rs 117.7 cr net. Spread over the stated execution windows (Rs 10.71 cr by Mar-2027, Rs 13.88 cr by Sep-2027, Rs 40.25 cr by Dec-2028) it supports the Rs 100-117 cr FY27 range above only if the older book converts quickly; the Dec-2028 order mostly lands in FY28 and FY29. **The Rs 40.25 cr order is an FY28-FY29 revenue event, not an FY27 one**, and the filing says so.

**What the order study says about this filing.** The 1,245-filing study in this repo (runbook 144c) measured two things that work:

| Test | This filing | What the study measured |
|---|---|---|
| Order / trailing year of sales | Rs 40.25 cr / Rs 84.11 cr = **47.9%** | The 25-50%-of-sales bucket reached 2x within two years **35.7%** of the time, against 21.4% for orders under 10% |
| Prior order filings in two years | **12** (13 including this one, read from BSE 30-Aug-2024 to 29-Sep-2026) | A first-filing-in-two-years reached 2x 30.4% and 5x 3.5%; a filer with **8 or more prior filings reached 2x only 17.3% and 5x never** |
| Market cap | Rs 1,931.7 cr | The Rs 300-7,500 cr band is where 5x runs happened; nothing above Rs 25,000 cr produced one in three years |

So the two halves of the test disagree, and the disagreement is the point: **the size is in the best bucket, the rarity is in the worst one.** Valiant files orders regularly — 13 in 760 days. On the study's rarity dimension alone this is a serial filer, and serial filers produced no 5x in three years.

ideas.red_flags:
- **Serial filer.** 13 order filings in 760 days. On the rarity half of the order study this is the bucket that reached 2x only 17.3% of the time and 5x never. This is the single biggest argument against reading today's filing as a step change.
- **The confirmed order book has been shrinking for five straight quarters** — Rs 101.95 cr (Q4 FY25) to Rs 64.20 cr (Q1 FY27), the company's own disclosure. Today's order reverses the direction; one order does not establish a trend, and the Q2 FY27 update (due with the November results) is the first honest test.
- **The customer is an intermediary, not the utility.** Today's award, and the 10-Sep and 27-Feb ones, come from a **"System Integrator (Private)"** whose name the company does not disclose. Valiant is a sub-supplier. That means no visibility on who the integrator is, what its own contract terms are, or what happens if the prime contract slips — and it means concentration risk that cannot be measured from the filings.
- **The pipeline figures are not orders and the company says so.** Beside the Rs 64.20 cr confirmed book, the Q1-FY27 update prints "L1 Status + Advanced Opportunities (approx) Rs 6,048 lacs" and "Forthcoming Business Opportunities (estimated) Rs 12,250 lacs", with an explicit note that these *"may change ... and should not be construed as confirmed orders"*. Treat only the Rs 64.20 cr as an order book.
- **Valuation.** Trailing PE 76.4 against the one available peer at 46.8; PB 35.3; the stock is +155.6% over one year, +44.6% in a month, and closed today at its 52-week high. Any disappointment is being priced off a high base.
- **A volume explosion is not evidence.** 7.2x the 60-day median today. The repo's own three-year study found 81% of 5x runs had a 10x volume day near the base — and so did 78% of the stocks that went nowhere.
- **Dilution above the current holders.** 6,00,000 warrants were issued at Rs 768 to the **non-promoter** category in the previous financial year; 2,50,000 converted on 07-May-2026 and **3,50,000 remain outstanding**. Who holds them is not stated in any document read this run.
- **Auditor and related party:** the FY2026 annual report lists revenue recognition as a key audit matter (Rs 8,411.37 lacs, "significant according to size of the Company") and states related-party transactions were at arm's length in the ordinary course with none requiring shareholder approval. No qualification or auditor change was found in the text read. The consolidated FY26 profit in the Directors' Report (Rs 2,418.07 lacs) is higher than the standalone Rs 2,166 lacs in the results; the subsidiaries (Valiant Communications UK, Valcomm USA, Valiant Infrastructure) account for the difference and their individual accounts were not read.
- **No concall, no investor presentation beyond the quarterly business update** was found in the 240-day filing list. The business update is a company-written document, not an audited one.
ideas.verify:
1. **Who the "System Integrator (Private)" is.** Three of the last four orders come from an unnamed private integrator. Identifying it — from a tender portal award, a PGCIL/state-transco EPC package list, or the integrator's own filings if listed — would say whether this is one relationship or several, and whether the Rs 40.25 cr is a slice of a much larger substation package. Only a tender-portal search or a call to the company can settle it.
2. **The Q2 FY27 gross order book.** The company publishes it every quarter with the results (due November 2026). It is the one number that tells you whether the five-quarter decline has genuinely turned. Nothing else in this note substitutes for it.

Whether the Rs 40.25 cr order is margin-accretive (supply + AMC) or dilutive (services drag) is not stated in the filing, and no capacity or utilisation figure appears in any document read. 4. **Who holds the 3,50,000 outstanding warrants** at Rs 768, and the identity of the "public category investors" in the preferential issue. The postal-ballot voting results of 13-Mar-2026 and the preferential-issue committee minutes would say; neither was read this run.

ideas.name: Indo Borax & Chemicals Ltd
ideas.trigger: filing: DEAL - Indo Borax filed a Reg 30 disclosure on 29-Sep-2026 15:44 IST that it has COMPLETED the acquisition of 2,38,44,000 equity shares of Kronox Lab Sciences Ltd (BSE 544187), 64.26% of Kronox's paid-up capital, for Rs 246.12 cr at Rs 103.22 per share, funded by a Rs 225 cr loan availed on 23-Sep-2026. A mandatory open offer for a further 25.79% follows.
ideas.thesis:
**The filings, read.** Three documents, all Reg 30, all filed by Indo Borax itself:

1. **20-Aug-2026 (board outcome).** The board approved a share purchase agreement among Indo Borax (the Purchaser), **Zenrock Chemicals Private Limited**, and the three selling promoters of Kronox — **Mr Ketan Vinodchandra Ramani, Mr Pritesh Vinodchandra Ramani, Mr Jogindersingh Gianchand Jaswal** — for **2,38,44,000 equity shares** of Rs 10 face value, **64.26%** of Kronox Lab Sciences Limited, at **Rs 103.22 per share**, aggregate **Rs 2,46,11,77,680**. The filing adds a footnote: the per-share price **including the consultancy fees payable by the target to each seller** under transition-support arrangements, computed per Regulation 8(7) of the SAST Regulations, is **Rs 105.87**.
2. Same filing, item 2: because control and more than 25% of voting capital pass, Indo Borax **with Zenrock as a person acting in concert** must make a **mandatory open offer for up to 95,70,000 shares, about 25.79%** of Kronox, at a price determined under the SAST Regulations.
3. **24-Sep-2026.** The company "has availed funding of **Rs 225 crore** ... from a lending institution on 23rd September, 2026 for the purpose of financing the acquisition of equity shares of Kronox Lab Sciences Limited". The lender is not named and no rate or tenor is stated.
4. **29-Sep-2026 (today).** "the said acquisition ... has been completed today, i.e., on September 29, 2026."

The accompanying press release (20-Aug-2026) adds that the erstwhile Kronox promoters **retain 9.95%** and provide transition support, and quotes MD & CEO Suresh Kalra on "expansion, diversification, premiumisation, and margin improvement".

**What each business physically does.**

- **Indo Borax & Chemicals** (Mumbai-registered, plant at Pithampur) is one of India's leading makers of **boron-based chemicals** — boric acid and derivatives. The FY2026 annual report describes a new **Boron Oxide facility at Pithampur with a planned capacity of 4,000 MTPA**, "enabling us to move further up the value chain into higher-margin Boron chemistry products", and states an ambition to be a "Boron chemistry company of global relevance".
- **Kronox Lab Sciences** (incorporated 2008, Vadodara, listed 2024) manufactures **high-purity specialty fine chemicals** for diversified end-user industries, across multiple manufacturing units in Gujarat.

Both are inorganic-chemistry businesses selling purified salts; the overlap is real, and the stated logic — export reach and margin — is plausible. Neither company has published a synergy number, and this note does not invent one.

**The measurable fact this filing creates.** Indo Borax has bought 64.26% of a listed company for Rs 246.12 cr. What that stake is worth is not a matter of opinion — Kronox trades, and the BSE bhavcopy prices it:

| | Rs |
|---|---:|
| Kronox close, 29-Sep-2026 | 217.20 |
| Kronox close, 19-Aug-2026 (day before the SPA was announced) | 155.30 |
| SPA price per share | 103.22 |
| SPA price incl. consultancy fees (SAST Reg 8(7)) | 105.87 |

| | Rs cr |
|---|---:|
| Kronox market cap at today's close (3.7106 cr shares) | 805.9 |
| The 64.26% stake, marked to today's close | 517.9 |
| What Indo Borax paid | 246.12 |
| **Difference** | **+271.8** |
| As a share of Indo Borax's own market cap (Rs 1,572.1 cr) | **+17.3%** |

Against the pre-announcement close of Rs 155.30 the stake is worth Rs 370.4 cr and the gap is Rs 124.3 cr. Either way, **control of Kronox changed hands well below the traded price** — Rs 103.22 against Rs 155.30 the day before the announcement, a 33.5% discount, and against Rs 217.20 today, a 52.5% discount. That is unusual: control normally carries a premium. **Why the sellers accepted it is not explained in any document read this run**, and it is the first thing on the verify list.

**The SPA multiple.** Rs 246.12 cr for 64.26% values Kronox at **Rs 383.0 cr**, which on Kronox's own audited FY2026 numbers is **13.8x PAT** and **3.78x sales**. Kronox's traded multiple, from the BSE header the same day, is **28.21x**.
ideas.model:
**Kronox, from its own BSE results filings** (Rs cr):

| Period | Revenue | PAT | EPS Rs |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| FY2025 (Apr-24 to Mar-25) | 100.19 | 25.31 | 6.91 |
| FY2026 (Apr-25 to Mar-26) | 101.22 | 27.66 | 7.51 |
| Q1 FY26 (Jun-25) | 24.29 | 6.28 | 1.70 |
| Q1 FY27 (Jun-26) | 28.39 | 7.30 | 2.00 |

Revenue was **flat** between FY25 and FY26 (+1.0%); PAT grew 9.3% on margin. Q1 FY27 revenue +16.9% YoY, PAT +16.2%. Net margin 27.3% in FY26. Finance cost near zero (Rs 1.14 cr for the full year) — Kronox is effectively debt-free.

**Indo Borax, standalone, from its own filings** (Rs cr):

| Period | Revenue | PAT | Finance cost |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| FY2025 | 175.26 | 41.88 | n/a |
| FY2026 | 215.45 | 49.74 | 0.66 |
| Q1 FY26 (Jun-25) | 53.57 | 10.04 | 0.00 |
| Q1 FY27 (Jun-26) | 70.36 | 16.26 | 0.49 |

FY26 revenue **+22.9%**, PAT **+18.8%**; Q1 FY27 revenue **+31.3%** YoY, PAT **+62.0%**. FY26 effective tax rate, from the results, **24.4%** (tax Rs 160.70 lacs on PBT Rs 658.10 lacs, as filed in Rs lacs). Finance cost of Rs 0.66 cr on Rs 215 cr of revenue means the company went into this deal **essentially debt-free**, with Rs 14.72 cr of other income in FY26 pointing to a sizeable treasury.

**What the deal adds, and what it costs. Show the arithmetic.**

| Line | Rs cr |
|---|---:|
| Kronox FY2026 PAT | 27.66 |
| Attributable to Indo Borax at 64.26% | **17.77** |
| Kronox Q1 FY27 PAT annualised, attributable | 18.76 |
| Interest on Rs 225 cr at 8.5% / 9.5% / 10.5% | 19.1 / 21.4 / 23.6 |
| The same after tax at Indo Borax's measured 24.4% rate | **14.4 / 16.2 / 17.8** |
| **Net first-full-year effect on consolidated PAT** | **+3.4 / +1.6 / -0.1** |

**The rate is not disclosed** — the 8.5-10.5% band is an assumption, stated as one. Within it, the acquisition is **roughly earnings-neutral in its first full year**. The purchase price carries an attributable earnings yield of 17.77 / 246.12 = **7.2%**, against an after-tax cost of debt of 6.4-7.9% on the borrowed portion. This is not an accretion story on year-one numbers.

Two further points the arithmetic forces:

- **FY2027 consolidates only half a year.** Completion was 29-Sep-2026, so roughly H2 FY27 carries Kronox. Consolidation brings **100% of Kronox's revenue** (Rs ~101 cr a year) into the top line with **35.74% shown as minority interest** below.
- **The open offer is a second, larger cheque and its price is unknown.** Up to 95,70,000 shares at a SAST-determined price. At the SPA price of Rs 105.87 that is Rs 101.3 cr; at today's traded Rs 217.20 it would be Rs 207.9 cr. **The public announcement stating the offer price was not read this run** (see the X section — a figure circulating there is recorded as unverified). If fully taken up the holding rises to about 90.05%, lifting attributable FY26 PAT to Rs 24.9 cr but adding the funding cost of another Rs 100-200 cr.

**What the study says about a filing like this.** The repo's order study (runbook 144c) measures **order** filings, and this is an acquisition, so its buckets do not apply directly. Two of its findings do:

| Test | Indo Borax |
|---|---|
| Market cap band where 5x runs happened (Rs 300-7,500 cr) | Rs 1,572.1 cr — inside it |
| Volume explosion as evidence | 5.6x the 60-day median today, +2.5% close. The study found 81% of 5x runs had a 10x volume day near the base and so did 78% of the stocks that went nowhere. It is not evidence |

The deal's size against sales is the honest scale marker: **Rs 246.12 cr paid against Rs 215.45 cr of FY2026 revenue** — the company has spent more than a year's turnover, most of it borrowed, on a single transaction.
ideas.valuation:
**Trailing, measured at the 29-Sep-2026 close of Rs 489.90.**

| | Indo Borax | Kronox (the target) |
|---|---:|---:|
| Close 29-Sep-2026, Rs | 489.90 | 217.20 |
| Shares, cr | 3.209 | 3.711 |
| Market cap, Rs cr | 1,572.1 | 805.9 |
| Trailing 4-quarter PAT, Rs cr | 55.96 | 29.19 |
| Trailing EPS, Rs | 17.44 | 7.70 |
| **Trailing PE** | **28.1** | **28.2** |
| BSE header same day (PE / PB / ROE / NPM) | 28.09 / 5.00 / 17.80 / - | 28.21 / 10.45 / 37.03 / 25.73 |

Our trailing-PAT arithmetic reproduces both BSE headers to the second decimal, which is the check that both share counts are right.

**The two companies trade at the same multiple, and Indo Borax bought control of the other at 13.8x.** That is the whole valuation argument in one line. It does not follow that the market is wrong — a 64.26% stake in a subsidiary is not the same asset as a free float, minority interest sits below the line, and Rs 225 cr of new debt now sits above it.

**A crude sum of the parts**, stated as arithmetic and not as a target:

| | Rs cr |
|---|---:|
| Indo Borax standalone, at its own trailing PE 28.1 on standalone TTM PAT Rs 55.96 cr | 1,572 |
| Kronox stake at market (64.26% of Rs 805.9 cr) | 518 |
| Less acquisition debt | (225) |
| Less the residual cash paid from own funds (246.12 - 225) | (21) |
| Sum | 1,844 |
| Current market cap | 1,572 |

The Rs 272 cr difference is exactly the mark-to-market gap on the stake, and it assumes the market's own price for Kronox is the right one. If the traded price of Kronox is what the control block is actually worth, the market has not yet marked it into Indo Borax; if the Rs 103.22 the sellers accepted is closer to fair value, there is no gap at all. **This note cannot tell you which, and does not pretend to.**

**Peers.** No peer table was built. BSE classifies Indo Borax under Commodity Chemicals and Kronox under Specialty Chemicals, and the site's industry index for either returns a list too heterogeneous (bulk commodity chemicals against high-purity fine chemicals) to compare multiples honestly from the files read this run.

**Balance sheet.** Before this deal Indo Borax carried essentially no debt (FY26 finance cost Rs 0.66 cr) and meaningful other income (Rs 14.72 cr in FY26). It now carries **Rs 225 cr** of acquisition debt against FY26 PAT of Rs 49.74 cr — about 4.5x one year's standalone profit. The specific balance-sheet lines (cash, borrowings, receivables at 31-Mar-2026) could not be extracted: the annual-report PDF's financial statements are an image-quality scan whose OCR output is unusable for those tables, and this note does not guess at numbers it could not read.

**Ownership, and the fact behind it.** Indo Borax's own promoter holding moved **50.80% (Jun-25, Sep-25, Dec-25) -> 30.80% (Mar-26) -> 38.41% (Jun-26)**. The FY2026 annual report names **Zenrock Chemicals Private Limited** as Acquirer, with India Special Assets Fund III, ISAF III Onshore Fund and Special Situation India Fund as Purchasers, undertaking an open offer for up to 83,43,400 shares (26%) of Indo Borax, and SAST Reg 29(2) disclosures for Zenrock were filed in May 2026 with a post-offer advertisement on 04-May-2026. **Indo Borax itself changed control earlier in 2026**, and the Kronox acquisition is the new owner's first major move. That is the frame the whole idea sits in.
ideas.red_flags:
- **Rs 225 cr of new debt on a company that had none.** FY26 finance cost was Rs 0.66 cr. The lender, the rate and the tenor are all undisclosed. On the 8.5-10.5% band used above, the after-tax interest alone eats between 81% and 100% of the attributable Kronox profit in a full year.
- **The deal is roughly EPS-neutral in year one on the numbers as filed.** The case rests on Kronox growing, on synergies neither company has quantified, and on the debt coming down — none of which is in a document yet.
- **Control bought at a large discount to the traded price, with no explanation on file.** Rs 103.22 against a Rs 155.30 close the day before the SPA and Rs 217.20 today. A control block sold 33-52% below market is an anomaly. Possible readings — an illiquid stock whose screen price is not a clearing price, seller-specific circumstances, terms in the SPA not in the public filing — cannot be told apart from what was read. Treat the Rs 272 cr paper gap with that caveat.
- **The open offer is an unpriced obligation.** Up to Rs 101 cr (at the SPA price) to Rs 208 cr (at today's price) of further cash, and the public announcement was not read this run. How it is funded is unknown.
- **Kronox's revenue was flat FY25 to FY26** (Rs 100.19 cr to Rs 101.22 cr). Profit grew on margin, not volume. Q1 FY27 turned up (+16.9%), one quarter.
- **The sellers stay involved.** The erstwhile promoters keep 9.95% and are paid **consultancy fees** for transition support — fees large enough to move the SAST-computed per-share price from Rs 103.22 to Rs 105.87, i.e. about Rs 6.3 cr in aggregate across 2,38,44,000 shares. A related-party arrangement with departing sellers is worth watching in the FY27 accounts.
- **A change of control in the acquirer itself, eight months old.** Zenrock Chemicals and three funds took control of Indo Borax in H1 2026; promoter holding is 38.41%, down from 50.80% a year ago. New owners doing debt-funded M&A within months is a pattern that can go either way, and there is no track record yet to judge.
- **The stock has already moved:** +113.4% over one year, +102.1% over six months, +28.9% over three months, closing today Rs 24.60 below its 52-week high of Rs 514.50. Volume today 5.6x the 60-day median — an alarm bell, not evidence.
- **No balance sheet, no rating report, no concall.** The annual report's financial statements could not be read (scan quality); no credit-rating filing appears in the 240-day announcement list.
ideas.verify:
1. **The open offer's public announcement and its price.** It determines a cash obligation of roughly Rs 100-208 cr and is filed with the exchanges by the manager to the offer. Reading it — the detailed public statement and the letter of offer — is the single most valuable next step, and it will also state how the offer is being funded (escrow, bank guarantee, the lender).
2. **The terms of the Rs 225 cr facility.** Lender, rate, tenor, security, covenants. The filing gives none of it. A rating rationale on the facility, if one is issued, would carry all of it plus the rating agency's own view of the combined entity's cash flows.
3. **Why the sellers accepted Rs 103.22.** The share purchase agreement is not public, but the letter of offer must set out the negotiated price and the SAST computation, and Kronox's own liquidity (55,296 shares traded today; 12,919 on 19-Aug-2026) may be much of the answer. Whether the screen price of a thinly traded 2024 listing is a clearing price for a control block is exactly the question.
4. **Kronox's plant-level economics.** Multiple units in Gujarat, high-purity fine chemicals, 27% net margin on flat revenue. What its capacity and utilisation are, and whether the Rs 101 cr revenue ceiling is demand or capacity, would need Kronox's own annual report and a site or customer check. None of that was read this run.
ideas.unknowns:
- Open offer price and its funding. Not read.
- Interest rate, tenor, security and lender of the Rs 225 cr facility.

- Any quantified synergy. Neither company has published one.

- The aggregate consultancy fee to the selling promoters, its schedule and its accounting treatment. Rs ~6.3 cr is implied by the Rs 103.22 / Rs 105.87 gap across 2,38,44,000 shares; the filing does not state the amount directly.

ideas.confidence: medium: every number in the trigger - 2,38,44,000 shares, 64.26%, Rs 103.22, Rs 246,11,77,680, Rs 225 cr of debt, completion today - is read field-by-field from Indo Borax's own Reg 30 filings, and both companies' financials come from their own BSE results, so the arithmetic is solid.
