ideas.name: Jyoti Structures Ltd
ideas.trigger: govt: Green Energy Corridor Phase-III - the Union Cabinet approved GEC-III on 30-Sep-2026 with a total outlay our own govt.py read as Rs 1,86,405 crore from the PIB release body, for intra-State transmission plus Battery Energy Storage. Jyoti Structures is a transmission-tower-and-EPC contractor whose FY2026 annual report names Green Energy Corridors and BESS as its stated demand drivers, carries a Rs 2,274 cr order book at 1-Apr-2026, and grew Q1 FY27 total income 57.1% YoY - while the stock sits 41.0% below where it was a year ago.
ideas.thesis:
**The decision, and how we read it.** On 30-Sep-2026 the Union Cabinet approved the **Green Energy Corridor Phase-III** scheme "for Development of Intra-State Transmission System with Battery Energy Storage Systems" (PIB release PRID 2316948, Cabinet). This repo's own `govt.py`, running from GitHub Actions at 18:56 IST that evening, opened the release body and recorded the outlay as **Rs 1,86,405 crore** with decision verb "approves" — the figure is our builder's parse of the PIB body, not a press summary, and it is the one number here traceable to a primary document read by this pipeline.

**What could not be read, and is therefore labelled.** `pib.gov.in` and `pmindia.gov.in` are both blocked by this sandbox's egress proxy, so the release body itself could not be opened this run. A web search of the official release returns a split of **Rs 1,36,378 cr for intra-State transmission and Rs 50,000 cr for 50 GWh of BESS, with Central Financial Support of Rs 54,082 cr, targeted at FY2032-33, enabling evacuation of up to 135 GW of renewable energy**. Those sub-figures are a search summary of the official release, not a document we opened, and they do not quite reconcile: 1,36,378 + 50,000 = 1,86,378, against the 1,86,405 our builder read, a Rs 27 cr gap. The note uses the split only as context and flags it as unverified.

**Why this release and not the others.** `govt.py` kept **7 releases on 30-Sep-2026** (4 distinct, each duplicated in the file). Three of the four are not order-book events and the note discards them: MSP for Rabi crops (Rs 8.36 lakh crore), the Rs 5,547.99 cr PSS procurement of pulses and oilseeds, and a Rs 1,789.52 cr Delhi real-time traffic management scheme. The first two are **farmer price support — a household/producer subsidy, which is exactly the shape of PM Surya Ghar, the one basket in this repo's study that UNDERPERFORMED the market (1.8x against 2.0x)**. And the theme mapper tagged both of them "shipbuilding", a plain false positive, so their mapped company lists are meaningless and were ignored. GEC-III is the only one of the four whose money becomes a transmission order book.

**What the business physically does.** Jyoti Structures (incorporated 1974, Mumbai) describes itself in its own press releases as "a leading infrastructure and **power transmission** engineering, procurement, and construction (EPC) company". From the FY2025-26 annual report and its own Reg 30 filings:

- Transmission towers are fabricated and galvanised in-house: **Nashik total manufacturing capacity approximately 72,000 MT per annum**, with a second Nashik unit whose stated milestones include "enhanced capability for execution of the prestigious **800 kV HVDC transmission project awarded by Power Grid Corporation of India Limited**". A Raipur factory and an Igatpuri testing station and R&D centre are also disclosed.
- Delivery is documented, not asserted: it filed **completion and commissioning of the 400 kV Gadag-II transmission line in Karnataka** (04-Mar-2026) — an intra-State line, which is the exact asset class GEC-III funds — and **completion and charging of a 400 kV multi-circuit LILO of Pirana (Torrent Power) to Pirana (POWERGRID)** (23-Feb-2026).
- International: a **Sri Lanka power transmission project** (press release 14-May-2026).
- The physical unit that drives revenue is a tonne of fabricated tower steel and a kilometre of line erected. The company publishes capacity in MT but **not utilisation, and not tonnes shipped**, so the tonnage model cannot be closed from the documents.

**The materiality link, in the company's own words.** The FY2026 annual report's outlook section names both components of GEC-III without being asked to: *"Green Energy Corridors, interstate transmission system expansion, smart grid deployment, and modernization of aging transmission assets are expected to generate significant EPC opportunities"*, and separately *"Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS) and smart grid solutions, which are expected to improve network reliability, operational efficiency and renewable energy integration"*. That is the playbook's test for a government-lane idea — the programme is material to this company by its own disclosure, not merely because it operates in the sector.
ideas.model:
**The order book is the disclosed driver.** From the FY2025-26 annual report, section "Operational Performance and Orders Book":

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Opening order book at 1-Apr-2026 | **Rs 2,274 cr** |
| FY26 total income | Rs 772.44 cr |
| **Order book / FY26 income** | **2.94x** |
| Aggregate total income, Resolution Plan (Nov-2021) to 31-Mar-2026 | Rs 1,974 cr |
| Major FY26 orders: turnkey EPC, 765 kV & 800 kV AC and HVDC lines + 765 kV substations | Rs 639.08 cr |
| Nashik fabrication capacity | ~72,000 MT per annum |

Note the second line against the third: the company has booked **Rs 1,974 cr of income in the four and a half years since its Resolution Plan**, and is carrying an order book of **Rs 2,274 cr**. The book is larger than everything it has billed since emerging from insolvency.

**Measured results.** From the BSE detailed-results feed and the company's own results press releases (standalone):

| Period | Total income Rs cr | EBITDA Rs cr | EBITDA % | PBT Rs cr | Net profit Rs cr |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| FY2024-25 | 504.50 | 44.28 | 8.78 | 35.66 | 35.81 |
| FY2025-26 | 772.44 | 69.97 | 9.06 | 54.72 | 56.04 |
| **Growth** | **+53.1%** | **+58.0%** | +28 bps | **+53.4%** | **+56.5%** |
| Q1 FY2025-26 | 162.40 | 13.14 | 8.09 | 10.24 | 11.16 |
| **Q1 FY2026-27** | **255.18** | **24.97** | **9.79** | **19.27** | **19.46** |
| **Growth** | **+57.1%** | **+90.0%** | **+169 bps** | **+88.2%** | **+74.4%** |

Revenue from operations (excluding other income) grew from Rs 156.16 cr to **Rs 251.46 cr, +61.0% YoY** in Q1 FY27. Margin is expanding at the same time as revenue, which is the combination the repo's earnings study found in 73.9% of its 5x runs (profit doubling) against 8.8% of the also-rans.

**One accounting feature to understand before reading the EPS.** Net profit **exceeds** PBT in both FY26 (Rs 56.04 cr vs Rs 54.72 cr) and Q1 FY27 (Rs 19.46 cr vs Rs 19.27 cr). A company that emerged from insolvency carries accumulated losses, so cash tax is minimal and a deferred-tax credit can push reported PAT above PBT. **This means the headline earnings are not fully taxed earnings**, and a normalised tax rate would cut them materially. No document read this run states the remaining carried-forward loss, so the size of that cushion is unknown.

**Forward revenue, from the disclosed book.** Rs 2,274 cr of order book against a Q1 FY27 run-rate of Rs 255.18 cr a quarter (Rs 1,021 cr annualised) is **2.2 years of work at the current pace**. Three arithmetic cases, with the quarterly run-rate held or grown:

| Sequential growth | FY27 total income Rs cr | Net profit at 7.0% | Net profit at 7.6% | EPS at 7.6% Rs | PE at Rs 8.91 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 0% (Q1 run-rate held) | 1,021 | 71.5 | 77.6 | 0.65 | 13.7 |
| +5% a quarter | 1,100 | 77.0 | 83.6 | 0.70 | 12.7 |
| +10% a quarter | 1,184 | 82.9 | 90.0 | 0.75 | 11.8 |

The 7.0-7.6% net margin band is the measured FY26 (7.26% of total income) and Q1 FY27 (7.63%) outcome and is an assumption carried forward, **not guidance — the company issues none in any document read this run**. Share count 119.365 cr (1,193,651,437 shares, from the 30-Jun-2026 shareholding filing). These cases assume the same lightly-taxed profit; they are not normalised.

**What the order study says about this name.** Jyoti filed **5 order-type disclosures in the 760 days to 2026-09-24** (23-Jan-2025 PowerGrid notification of award, then "Intimation on New Project Order" on 25-Feb-2025, 15-Oct-2025, 30-Mar-2026 and 13-May-2026; BSE read complete, 158 filings). The study measured the two ends: a company filing its **first** order in two years reached 2x 30.4% of the time and 5x 3.5%; one with **8 or more** prior filings reached 2x 17.3% and 5x **never**. Five puts Jyoti between the measured extremes, and the study gives no bucket for exactly five — so the honest statement is that it is neither the rare filer the study rewards nor the serial bidder it penalises. Market cap Rs 1,063.5 cr sits inside the Rs 300-7,500 cr band where every 5x run in three years occurred.
ideas.valuation:
**Trailing, at the 2026-10-01 close of Rs 8.91** (BSE bhavcopy: close 8.91, previous 8.92, 408,920 shares, turnover Rs 36.0 lakh).

| | Jyoti Structures |
|---|---:|
| Market cap | Rs 1,063.5 cr |
| Shares | 119.365 cr |
| Trailing 4-quarter PBT (Q2 FY26 - Q1 FY27) | Rs 62.59 cr |
| Trailing EPS on that basis | Rs 0.524 |
| **Trailing PE** | **17.0** |
| BSE header same day (EPS / PE / PB / ROE) | 0.54 / 16.50 / 6.96 / 42.10 |
| Order book / market cap | 2.14x |
| Price vs 52-week range (high 15.32, low 7.97) | 41.8% below the high, 11.8% above the low |
| Returns 1m / 3m / 6m / 1y | -9.8% / -25.9% / -15.1% / **-41.0%** |

Our arithmetic and BSE's header agree to within a rounding step, which is the check that the 119.365 cr share count is right.

**PB of 6.96 against ROE of 42.10 is the tension in this name.** Both are BSE's own header figures for 2026-10-04. A 42% return on equity on a post-insolvency balance sheet reflects a very small equity base relative to the revenue it turns, not a durable franchise return — and it is the same lightly-taxed profit noted above. The book value this PB is measured against is small for the same reason.

**The re-rating case, in one sentence.** The stock is 41% lower than a year ago while total income grew 53% and the order book is 2.9x revenue; if the Rs 2,274 cr book converts at the Q1 FY27 margin the trailing 17x becomes roughly 12-14x forward, and GEC-III adds Rs 1.36 lakh crore of intra-State transmission tendering to the pipeline it bids into.

**Peers: not available.** The site's industry index for "Heavy Electrical Equipment" returned Kamdhenu, Commercial Syn Bags, Nelcast, Hariom Pipe, Bharat Wire Ropes, GRP, R M Drip and Borosil Scientific — companies matched by market cap, not by business. **No honest peer multiple table could be built from the files read this run**, and the note does not invent one. The listed transmission-EPC comparables (KEC International, Kalpataru, Transrail, Skipper, Bajel) sit outside the Rs 200-2,000 cr universe and were not priced this run.

**Balance sheet.** The FY26 annual report names "non-fund-based limits, working capital management" first in its risk list, and the company filed an initial disclosure as a **"Large Corporate"** (14-Apr-2026), the SEBI category for entities with substantial outstanding long-term borrowing. A **Rights Issue II** was in progress in June 2026, with monitoring-agency reports filed for the quarter ended 31-Mar-2026 and again on 04-Aug-2026. **The specific debt, cash and receivable figures at 31-Mar-2026 were not extracted this run** and are listed under unknowns rather than estimated.

**Ownership - the single most unusual fact here, and a correction.** The dossier builder reported "promoter 100.0%" for every quarter. **That is a parser error and it is wrong.** Reading the 30-Jun-2026 shareholding XBRL page directly, the row the regex matched is **"(B) Public — 201,951 holders, 1,193,651,437 shares, 100.00%"**. Jyoti Structures has **no promoter**: the float is 100% public across 201,951 shareholders, with 8,500 shares (0.00%) in the non-promoter-non-public category. The Resolution Plan extinguished the former promoter group. Two consequences the note takes seriously: there is **no promoter skin in the game**, and the study's "promoter stake rose" signal (present in 15.2% of 5x runs) is structurally unavailable for this company. One block of **3,00,00,000 shares = 2.51%** appears in the same filing; the holder's identity is not established from any primary document read this run.
ideas.red_flags:
- **Lenders have taken the company to the NCLAT in contempt proceedings.** On 27-Feb-2026 Jyoti filed an "Intimation regarding appeal filed by lenders before NCLAT in contempt proceedings relating to disbursement of **non-fund-based limits**". For a transmission EPC contractor, non-fund-based limits are bank guarantees — the instrument required to bid and to draw advances. A dispute with lenders over their disbursement is close to existential for the order book, and it is the single biggest reason this idea is not high confidence. Further NCLT/NCLAT directions were filed on 18-Feb-2026 and 27-May-2026.
- **No promoter.** 100% public float, post-insolvency. Nobody is underwriting the equity, and there is no promoter whose buying would signal anything.
- **Earnings are not fully taxed.** Net profit exceeds PBT in both FY26 and Q1 FY27. The accumulated-loss cushion from insolvency is not quantified in anything read this run; when it runs out, reported EPS falls at a normalised rate even if operations are unchanged.
- **Governance churn in a single quarter.** The Chief Executive Officer **resigned** (29-May-2026); the Chairman and Independent Director **died** (17-Jul-2026); an internal auditor, Bhushan Khot & Co, was **appointed on 30-Apr-2026 and removed on 04-Aug-2026**, having been appointed on the same day as a second internal auditor (K N B J & Associates); and a **corrigendum to the FY2025-26 Annual Report** was filed on 27-Jul-2026. Each is individually explainable; together, in four months, they are a pattern worth weighing.
- **Dilution in progress.** Rights Issue II was live in June 2026 with monitoring-agency reporting. The share count used in this note (119.365 cr, at 30-Jun-2026) may already be stale, and the EPS cases above would scale down accordingly. The issue's size, price and utilisation were not read this run.
- **Thin trading.** Median 60-day turnover Rs 31.9 lakh on a Rs 1,063 cr company; 408,920 shares traded on 2026-10-01. A single-digit share price with this float makes the quoted price easy to move and hard to transact in size.
- **GEC-III is an opportunity to bid, not an order.** The scheme runs to FY2032-33 and is implemented by State transmission utilities, which tender separately. Nothing in it is Jyoti's until a State utility awards it, and the repo's own study found the baskets' bases came **months** after the policy date — the defence names bottomed between September and November 2020. There is no reason to treat 30-Sep-2026 as a starting gun.
- **The transmission basket's measured history is the weakest of the strong ones.** 47 companies from the FY23 capex cycle, median 4.7x against 3.0x for the market, 49% made 5x — real outperformance, but a fraction of defence (17.4x) or RDSS smart meters (12.0x). And nearly every winner in every basket is now 30-90% below its peak.
- **No concall, no investor presentation, no credit-rating report** appears in the 240-day filing list. The only management narrative is a one-page results press release, which is company-written.
- **The 2.51% block is unattributed.** A named investor would be a data point; an unidentified 3 crore-share holder is not.
ideas.verify:
1. **The NCLAT non-fund-based-limits proceeding.** Its current status and what the lenders are actually withholding is the one fact that most changes this idea. The NCLAT order itself, and the contingent-liability and "going concern"/emphasis-of-matter notes in the FY26 audited accounts, would settle it. Neither was read this run.
2. **The remaining carried-forward tax loss.** It determines whether reported EPS is repeatable. It sits in the tax note of the FY26 financial statements.
3. **Rights Issue II: size, price, subscription and the resulting share count.** The letter of offer and the allotment intimation would give all four, and would correct every per-share figure in this note.
4. **Tonnes shipped and Nashik utilisation.** Capacity is disclosed at ~72,000 MT per annum; output is not. Without it the tonnage-based revenue model cannot be closed, and only a plant visit, a concall or a customer check would give it.

ideas.confidence: low: the government decision is real and large, and the materiality link is unusually clean - Jyoti's own annual report names Green Energy Corridors and BESS as its demand drivers, it has commissioned an intra-State 400 kV line, and it carries a disclosed Rs 2,274 cr order book that is 2.9x FY26 income while the stock is 41% below a year ago. What holds this at low rather than medium is not the thesis but the balance sheet and the register: lenders are at the NCLAT in contempt proceedings over the non-fund-based limits an EPC contractor cannot bid without, the company has no promoter at all, reported profit exceeds PBT because insolvency losses shelter it, a rights issue is diluting, and the CEO left, the chairman died and an internal auditor was removed inside four months.

ideas.name: Solarworld Energy Solutions Ltd
ideas.trigger: govt: Green Energy Corridor Phase-III - the Cabinet approved GEC-III on 30-Sep-2026, outlay Rs 1,86,405 cr as parsed from the PIB body by our own govt.py, covering intra-State transmission AND Battery Energy Storage. Solarworld has already won and disclosed 257 MW / 514 MWh of NTPC BESS EPC work worth Rs 599.39 cr at Rs 1.08-1.19 cr per MWh. The filing that put it on the list is the 30-Sep-2026 Reg 30 disclosure of a Rs 78.75 cr purchase order for 96,000 G12R 625 Wp panels (60 MW) won by its wholly owned module subsidiary.
ideas.thesis:
**Two things happened on 30-Sep-2026** and only together do they make an idea. The Cabinet approved **Green Energy Corridor Phase-III** — outlay **Rs 1,86,405 crore** as read from the PIB release body by this repo's `govt.py` — a scheme whose own title is "Development of Intra-State Transmission System **with Battery Energy Storage Systems**". And Solarworld filed a Reg 30 disclosure that its wholly owned subsidiary had received a purchase order for solar panels. The order is small. The BESS franchise behind it is not.

**The order, read.** From the filing (BSE, 30-Sep-2026 13:28 IST; event occurred 29-Sep-2026 18:06): **ZNShine Solarworld Private Limited**, a wholly owned subsidiary, received a purchase order from "a leading renewable energy player" (unnamed, domestic) for **96,000 solar panels, model G12R 625 Wp, at a unit price of Rs 7,812.50**, giving a **basic order value of Rs 75.00 crore and a total of Rs 78.75 crore including 5% IGST**. No execution period is stated beyond "as per terms and conditions mentioned in purchase order". Not a related-party transaction.

That filing is unusually complete, and it closes a physical model exactly:

| Step | Arithmetic | Result |
|---|---|---:|
| Panels x wattage | 96,000 x 625 Wp | **60.0 MW** |
| Basic value / MW | Rs 75.00 cr / 60 MW | **Rs 1.25 cr per MW** |
| Playbook constant for non-DCR modules | — | Rs 1.3 cr per MW |

The realised price lands within 4% of the conversion constant this playbook carries for non-DCR modules — an independent check that the order is priced like a normal third-party module sale, not an inflated related-party print.

**Why the module order matters qualitatively more than Rs 78.75 cr suggests.** The FY2025-26 annual report discloses a **1.552 GW TOPCon module manufacturing facility commissioned at Roorkee, Uttarakhand, "producing high-efficiency modules of 600W-750W across the M10R, G12R and G12 formats"**. The order is for **G12R 625 Wp** — the exact format from that plant. The annual report also records ZNShine Solarworld as a wholly owned subsidiary transacting "sale of goods or materials" with the parent "pursuant to the Company's strategic backward integration initiative". So this is the step from captive backward integration to a **third-party module sale**, which is what turns a cost centre into a revenue line.

**What the business physically does** (all from the FY2025-26 annual report's own key-highlights page):

| Metric | Disclosed figure |
|---|---|
| Solar and renewable projects executed / under execution | 60+ |
| EPC portfolio installed | 348 MW DC |
| Ongoing solar EPC capacity | 1,809 MW DC |
| Module manufacturing (Roorkee, TOPCon) | 1.552 GW |
| Junction box manufacturing | 5 GW |
| **Ongoing BESS capacity** | **1,164 MWh** |
| BESS manufacturing facility | 3.4 GW |
| Solar cell facility | 2.4 GW "under development with proposed JV, targeted for commissioning by June 2027" |
| FY26 total income | Rs 14,160 mn (Rs 1,416 cr), up 157% YoY |
| FY26 PAT | Rs 1,204 mn (Rs 120.4 cr), up 56% YoY |

**The BESS franchise, from its own Reg 30 filings.** This is the part that connects to GEC-III, and every row is read from the filing itself:

| Filed | Awarding entity | Site | Capacity | Order value (excl. taxes) | Rs cr per MWh |
|---|---|---|---|---:|---:|
| 2026-03-29 | NTPC Limited | Solapur Super TPS, Lot-1 | 132 MW / 264 MWh | 314.26 | 1.19 |
| 2026-03-30 | NTPC Limited | Solapur Super TPS, Lot-2 | 75 MW / 150 MWh | 176.91 | 1.18 |
| 2026-03-30 | NTPC Limited | Feroze Gandhi Unchahar TPS, Lot-2 | 50 MW / 100 MWh | 108.22 | 1.08 |
| | | **Total** | **257 MW / 514 MWh** | **599.39** | **1.17 avg** |

All three are BESS Engineering, Procurement and Construction, 15 months to completion of facilities, same bid document CS-0011-171B-9. **The annual report independently states "BESS EPC orders worth Rs 5.99 billion for NTPC's Solapur and Unchahar thermal power station projects"** — Rs 599 cr, against the Rs 599.39 cr sum of the three individual filings. The two sources agree, which is the check that nothing is double-counted.

Separately, a **Balance of System package for Block-IX (200 MWac)** of a 1,000 MW grid-connected solar PV project at Bikaner, Rajasthan, from **NTPC Renewable Energy Limited**, with three years of O&M, 19 months (filed 01-Apr-2026). The filing's size field states only "200 MWac"; the annual report prices it at **Rs 2.35 billion (Rs 235 cr)**.

**The GEC-III cross-check, and its limit.** GEC-III provides, per the search summary of the official release, **Rs 50,000 crore for 50 GWh of BESS** — an implied **Rs 1.00 cr per MWh**. Solarworld's three realised NTPC awards price at **Rs 1.08-1.19 cr per MWh**. The government's implied rate and this company's realised rate are within 17% of each other, which says the scheme is budgeted at something like the price at which this company actually builds. Its 514 MWh of awarded work is **1.03% of the 50 GWh** the scheme funds, and its 1,164 MWh of ongoing BESS capacity is 2.33%. **That is arithmetic about scale, not a forecast of market share** — nothing entitles this company to any share of a scheme whose tenders have not been issued.
ideas.model:
**Measured results** (BSE detailed-results feed, standalone; the annual report's consolidated figures differ and are given separately):

| Period | Revenue Rs cr | Other income | Total income | PAT Rs cr | PAT / total income |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Q1 FY2025-26 (Jun-25) | 68.31 | 13.74 | 82.05 | 16.57 | 20.2% |
| Q2 FY26 (Sep-25) | 126.81 | 5.72 | 132.53 | 15.24 | 11.5% |
| Q3 FY26 (Dec-25) | 495.38 | 11.17 | 506.55 | 50.77 | 10.0% |
| Q4 FY26 (Mar-26) | 511.50 | 20.09 | 531.59 | 50.09 | 9.4% |
| **FY2025-26** | **1,202.00** | 50.71 | 1,252.72 | **132.67** | 10.6% |
| **Q1 FY2026-27 (Jun-26)** | **143.96** | 13.23 | **157.19** | **16.22** | **10.3%** |

Q1 FY27 revenue is **+110.8% YoY** on Q1 FY26's Rs 68.31 cr — but PAT is **-2.1%**, Rs 16.22 cr against Rs 16.57 cr, because the margin on total income **halved from 20.2% to 10.3%**. Read the quarterly column before reading the growth rate: revenue runs 68 / 127 / 495 / 512 / 144 across five quarters. That is EPC percentage-of-completion recognition, and it means **no single quarter of this company tells you anything about a run-rate.** The annual figures are the only honest base.

**Order book and visibility** (FY2025-26 annual report):

| Component | Rs cr |
|---|---:|
| Solar EPC and O&M projects | 1,674 |
| EPC and BESS IPP-related projects | 1,139 |
| **Total order book** | **2,813** |
| FY26 total income (consolidated, per AR) | 1,416 |
| **Order book / FY26 total income** | **1.99x** |
| Order book / market cap | **2.58x** |

**Forward revenue, three cases.** Rs 2,813 cr of book, with the BESS packages contracted at 15 months and the BOS package at 19 months, implies the bulk converts across FY27 and FY28. Taking FY26 total income of Rs 1,416 cr as the base:

| FY27 revenue growth | FY27 total income Rs cr | PAT at 9.4% | PAT at 10.6% | EPS at 10.6% Rs | PE at Rs 125.90 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 0% | 1,416 | 133.1 | 150.1 | 17.32 | 7.3 |
| +20% | 1,699 | 159.7 | 180.1 | 20.78 | 6.1 |
| -20% | 1,133 | 106.5 | 120.1 | 13.86 | 9.1 |

The 9.4-10.6% margin band is the measured Q4 FY26 and FY26 outcome. **The company issues no revenue or margin guidance in any document read this run**, so all three columns are arithmetic on stated history, not forecasts. Share count 8.667 cr (market cap Rs 1,091.2 cr / close Rs 125.90, cross-checked below). Note the **-20% case still prints a single-digit PE**, which is the point of the valuation section.

**What the order study says about the trigger filing.** The Rs 78.75 cr purchase order is **6.6% of FY26 standalone revenue (Rs 1,202 cr), 5.6% of consolidated total income (Rs 1,416 cr), and 2.8% of the order book**. The study measured order size against a trailing year of sales: **under 10% of sales reached 2x within two years 21.4% of the time, against 35.7% for the 25-50% bucket.** So on the one dimension the study found predictive, **this order sits in the weakest bucket.** It is the trigger that put the name on the list, not the reason to look at it.

On rarity it does better: **7 order-type filings in the 760 days to 2026-10-01** (BSE read complete, 117 filings) — below the 8-or-more threshold at which the study found 2x odds of 17.3% and **no 5x at all**. Market cap Rs 1,091.2 cr sits inside the Rs 300-7,500 cr band where every measured 5x run occurred.
ideas.valuation:
**Trailing, at the 2026-10-01 close of Rs 125.90** (BSE bhavcopy: close 125.90, previous 129.20, 46,466 shares, turnover Rs 59.72 lakh).

| | Solarworld |
|---|---:|
| Market cap | Rs 1,091.2 cr |
| Shares (market cap / close) | 8.667 cr |
| Trailing 4-quarter PAT (Q2 FY26 - Q1 FY27) | Rs 132.32 cr |
| Trailing EPS | **Rs 15.27** |
| **Trailing PE** | **8.24** |
| BSE header same day (EPS / PE) | **15.27 / 8.24** |
| Net worth at 31-Mar-2026 (AR) | Rs 845 cr |
| Implied price / book | **1.29x** |
| Debt / equity at 31-Mar-2026 (AR) | **0.3x** |
| Order book / market cap | 2.58x |
| Price vs 52-week range (high 338.70, low 125.90) | **at the 52-week low** |
| Returns 1m / 3m / 6m / 1y | -13.2% / -32.0% / -27.5% / **-62.2%** |

Our trailing EPS of Rs 15.27 reproduces BSE's header **exactly**, which is the check that the 8.667 cr share count is right.

**The whole valuation argument in three lines.** A company with Rs 2,813 cr of disclosed order book, Rs 845 cr of net worth, 0.3x debt-to-equity and Rs 132 cr of trailing profit is quoted at **Rs 1,091 cr — 8.2x trailing earnings and 1.29x book**, at its 52-week low, having fallen 62% in a year. Either the market is pricing the de-rating of an IPO that came too expensive, or it is pricing something about the earnings that this note has found part of (see red flags), or both.

**Why the stock fell 62%: the part that is measurable.** The share was listed in **September 2025** (X search results give an IPO price band of Rs 333-351 and a Rs 490 cr issue; the prospectus was not read this run, so treat the band as unverified). The 52-week high of Rs 338.70 is consistent with a listing near that band. At Rs 125.90 the stock is **62.8% below its 52-week high**. A substantial part of the fall is therefore the de-rating of a 2025 listing rather than a deterioration disclosed quarter by quarter — but the margin halving in Q1 FY27 and the dispute awards below are disclosed deteriorations, and both post-date the listing.

**Peers: not built.** BSE classifies Solarworld under "Civil Construction", which mixes it with road and building contractors that share none of its economics. The comparable listed solar-EPC and BESS names (Sterling & Wilson, Waaree, Premier Energies, KPI Green) sit outside the Rs 200-2,000 cr universe and were not priced this run. **No honest peer multiple table could be built from the files read**, and the note does not invent one.

**Ownership.** Promoter holding **65.77%** at both 31-Mar-2026 and 30-Jun-2026, from 65.67% at 31-Dec-2025 — stable to marginally rising, no pledge disclosed in anything read this run. Managing Director Kartik Teltia (DIN 06610105) signs the Reg 30 filings personally.
ideas.red_flags:
- **Rs 219.33 crore of claims against a client, of which only 18.4% was admitted.** On 18-Sep-2026 Solarworld disclosed the outcome of two Dispute Adjudication Board proceedings it had **itself invoked** against **SJVN Green Energy Limited** on the GUVNL Phase XIII (100 MW) and Phase XIV (260 MW) solar EPC contracts at Mothara, Kutch:

| Case | Claim heads | Claimed Rs cr | Awarded Rs cr | % admitted | of which cash |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 100 MW (DAB/100MW/01/2026) | 12 | 56.51 | 13.77 | 24.4% | 5.79 |
| 260 MW (DAB/260MW/01/2026) | 8 | 162.83 | 26.50 | 16.3% | 2.09 |
| **Total** | 20 | **219.33** | **40.27** | **18.4%** | **7.88** |

  The claim heads are the diagnostic: *release of retention monies, overdue supply invoices, delay financing interest, site preservation and module insurance costs, loss of profit*. That is a working-capital dispute, and Rs 219 cr of it on a company with Rs 1,202-1,416 cr of annual revenue. Most of what was awarded is **retention released against bank-guarantee or surety-bond substitution, not cash** — Rs 32.39 cr of the Rs 40.27 cr. This is the single most important thing found this run and it is not in any press summary.
- **Margin halved in the latest quarter.** PAT fell to 10.3% of total income in Q1 FY27 from 20.2% a year earlier, with revenue up 110.8%. Whether that is mix (module supply at lower margin than EPC), the dispute provisions, or price competition in solar EPC is **not explained in any document read this run.**
- **The trigger order is in the weakest bucket the study measured.** Rs 78.75 cr is 5.6-6.6% of a year's sales — the under-10% bucket, 21.4% odds of a 2x against 35.7% for a 25-50% order.
- **The customer is unnamed.** "A leading renewable energy player". No concentration, credit or terms assessment is possible, and the execution period is not stated at all.
- **Interest coverage has moderated.** The annual report states the ratio moderated "consequent to increased borrowings to support project execution, manufacturing expansion and business growth". Debt-to-equity of 0.3x is comfortable in isolation; the direction is the point, and the absolute debt figure was not extracted this run.
- **Revenue is violently lumpy.** 68 / 127 / 495 / 512 / 144 across five quarters. Any growth rate quoted off one quarter is noise, and a reader who annualises Q1 FY27 gets Rs 629 cr against FY26's Rs 1,416 cr.
- **The 2.4 GW cell plant is a proposal, not a project.** The annual report says "under development **with proposed JV**, targeted for commissioning by June 2027". A proposed JV has no partner named and no signed agreement disclosed in anything read this run.
- **A 2025 listing at its all-time low.** Down 62.2% in a year, closing exactly at the 52-week low of Rs 125.90. Nothing in the price action suggests a base has formed; the repo's own study found winners' bases came months after their trigger and that nearly every past winner is now 30-90% below its peak.
- **GEC-III is not an order.** 50 GWh of BESS is a budget line to FY2032-33, tendered by State utilities and agencies that have issued nothing yet. Solarworld's claim on it is a track record, not a contract.
- **Thin trading.** Median 60-day turnover Rs 27.3 lakh; 46,466 shares on 2026-10-01.
ideas.verify:
1. **What the margin halving actually is.** Q1 FY27 PAT margin of 10.3% against 20.2% is the number that decides whether the 8.2x multiple is cheap or correct. The Q1 FY27 investor presentation (filed 14-Aug-2026) and the Q4 FY26 earnings-call recording (26-May-2026) both exist in the filing list and **neither was read this run** — they are the first place to look, and this note's biggest gap.
2. **Receivables, retention and unbilled revenue at 31-Mar-2026.** The DAB claims were about retention monies and overdue supply invoices, so the balance-sheet lines behind them are the real story. They sit in the FY26 financial statements, which were not extracted this run.
3. **Whether the two X-sourced order claims exist at all.** Posts claim a **Rs 806 cr GUVNL BESS EPC order** and a **Rs 725.33 cr NTPC Renewable Energy 250 MWac solar order**. Neither appears anywhere in Solarworld's BSE filings over the 300 days read this run. If real they would transform the order book; if not, they are noise. The company's own website disclosures and the NSE filing feed would settle it.
4. **The IPO price, size and use of proceeds.** It frames the entire -62% move. The prospectus and the monitoring-agency reports would give it; neither was read.

ideas.confidence: medium-low: the BESS exposure is documented to an unusual depth - three NTPC awards read field by field, 257 MW / 514 MWh for Rs 599.39 cr, whose sum the annual report independently confirms at Rs 5.99 bn, priced at Rs 1.08-1.19 cr per MWh against the Rs 1.00 cr per MWh GEC-III implies for its 50 GWh - and the stock is 8.2x trailing earnings and 1.29x book with a Rs 2,813 cr order book, 2.58x its market cap. Three things keep it below medium: the trigger order is only 5.6-6.6% of a year's sales, the weakest bucket the order study measured; the Q1 FY27 margin halved and no document read this run explains why; and the company had to take its own client to a Dispute Adjudication Board over Rs 219 cr of retention and overdue invoices and recovered 18.4%, mostly as bank-guarantee substitution rather than cash.

- **A Rs 806 crore GUVNL BESS EPC order.** Searched Solarworld's BSE announcements across the 300 days to 2026-10-01 (117 filings, read complete): **no such order appears.** No filing read this run names Gujarat Urja Vikas Nigam as an awarding entity at all.

- **Directly, and it matters.** A post frames Gujarat/GUVNL as an Rs 806 cr **order win**. A reader taking the X posts at face value would have a materially more favourable picture of this company's Gujarat exposure than its own filings support.
- The posts are, as a set, order-announcement flow. **None mentions the DAB awards or the Q1 FY27 margin halving** — the two disclosed facts that most constrain this idea.
